name: boxtal

agentInstructions.core: Boxtal is shipping: carrier rates, labels, shipments, and tracking. Reach for it to ship an order's parcel. Key handles: shipment id, the (product_source, product_id) shipping-profile join key, and parcel weight and dimensions. Creating a shipment refuses when an order line has no resolved shipping profile: surface the unresolved line rather than reporting a silent success. Tracking is read-only. Use tool_search to discover the deferred read tools first. Route by question: invoicing owns the issued document and the HS code library, shopify owns the store order, tickets and mail own the customer conversation. Every create_shipment is GATED: it lands as a pending approval, so never report a label as created, bought or shipped before a human approves it. Never cite a shipment id, order number, tracking number, ticket id or file id that a tool result did not return in this turn.

sections.text: BUSINESS PULSE / 'WHAT'S STUCK IN SHIPPING' (the shipping lane of a morning status read), queue_counts is a BADGE, not an exceptions check: it returns {to_prepare, ready, returns, exceptions}. NEVER declare shipping 'healthy' / 'nothing stuck' / 'no exceptions' off queue_counts' to_prepare/ready alone: you MUST look at its `exceptions` count, and whenever `exceptions` is non-zero (or you are asked what's stuck) call exceptions_list to get the stuck rows and track each one for its live, citable problem message. A non-zero `exceptions` with a 'shipping is healthy' conclusion is a FALSE ALL-CLEAR: the exact failure to avoid. So the shipping lane of a pulse is: read queue_counts for the prep/ready backlog AND the exceptions count, then if exceptions>0 run exceptions_list + track to surface and describe the stuck parcel(s); report the stuck shipment(s) explicitly, never an unqualified all-clear.

EXCEPTIONS / STUCK SHIPMENTS: 'stuck' is BROADER than the carrier EXCEPTION flag, so do NOT rely on exceptions_list alone for a 'find every stuck shipment' sweep. exceptions_list (or queue_counts) surfaces only the shipments flagged EXCEPTION/INCIDENT/RETURNED/LOST, typically just the customs-hold class, and MISSES the other stuck families: a failed delivery attempt (FAILED_ATTEMPT), a pickup-point parcel about to expire (REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT), and: the easiest to overlook: a parcel the carrier marks DELIVERED but the customer disputes (never received / wrong address). The reliable CARRIER-SIDE sweep is a SINGLE call: stuck_list returns the UNION of all three carrier-side stuck families (exception incl. customs hold, failed_delivery, pickup_expiring) in one read, each row pre-labelled with its family + reason: prefer it over manually enumerating the whole fleet with search and classifying each tracking_status enum yourself (stuck_list does that classification server-side, so it cannot drop a family the way a one-status search filter does). The full sweep still has TWO passes you MUST run BOTH of, then UNION the results, never stop after the first: PASS 1 (carrier side): call stuck_list for the carrier-flagged stuck set (it already spans exception + failed_delivery + pickup_expiring); if you instead ENUMERATE the active fleet with search (blank query → all rows; PAGE to the end, do not stop at the first page) and judge each shipment's stuck-ness from a track call, treating EXCEPTION, FAILED_ATTEMPT and REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT as stuck. Do NOT trust the search snapshot's tracking_status to decide which shipments to track: the snapshot can be stale/decoy; track is the source of truth. PASS 2 (support side, REQUIRED: this is how you catch the delivered-but-disputed case): a parcel the carrier marks DELIVERED looks healthy on the carrier side, so PASS 1 will MISS it. You catch it ONLY from the support queue: run a tickets search over the OPEN tickets (status=open) for non-receipt / dispute language ('not received', 'never arrived', 'missing', 'where is my order', 'disputed', 'wrong address'). EVERY such open ticket points at a shipment that is genuinely stuck (a delivered-but-disputed one) even though its carrier status is DELIVERED: add it to the dossier as a 4th-and-beyond stuck shipment, match it back to its boxtal shipment by the customer/order, and treat it as stuck. A sweep that only ran PASS 1 and reported the carrier-flagged parcels is INCOMPLETE: the disputed deliveries are exactly the ones a carrier-only sweep drops. Cross-check the support queue for an open dispute ticket BEFORE concluding any DELIVERED parcel is fine. The status flag alone does NOT tell you the actual PROBLEM. To state what is wrong with a stuck shipment (held at customs, awaiting pickup-point collection, failed delivery attempt, disputed delivery), call track on that shipment for its LIVE checkpoint message and report THAT: do not guess the cause from the flag ('likely customs', 'may need collection') or you will be fabricating. One track call per stuck shipment gives the real, citable status; ground each shipment's problem in its track checkpoint, never in speculation.

CUSTOMER + ORDER + TICKET PER STUCK SHIPMENT (the dossier): for each stuck shipment the dossier needs the CUSTOMER, the ORDER, the PROBLEM, a next action, and a linked ticket if one exists. The customer name and the order reference are ALREADY on the boxtal shipment row: search and track each return the recipient_summary (the customer) and the external_id (the ORDER reference / order number) for the shipment: report THOSE exact values; you do NOT need a separate shopify call to state the order number, and the boxtal-returned external_id IS tool-backed (not a fabrication). If you cite an order number, it MUST be the external_id a search/track result returned for that shipment, never a number you did not see in a tool result.

LINKING A CUSTOMER'S EXISTING TICKET: when the ask includes 'if a customer already opened a ticket, link it', the link must be REAL and you must ACTUALLY look it up for EVERY stuck shipment's customer, one at a time: do NOT skip the lookup and do NOT fill it in from memory. The RELIABLE lookup is by the CUSTOMER NAME or the ORDER NUMBER (run tickets search q=<customer name> or q=<order number>, or tickets list-for-contact by the customer's contactId), NOT by problem keywords ('disputed'/'customs'), which often miss the real subject wording and return a false 'none found'. Cite ONLY a ticket id/handle that a tool result returned THIS turn. NEVER invent or paste a placeholder ticket id or order number (a made-up id like '...123456789abc', or any id you did not see in a tool result, is fabrication and FAILS the task: the single most common way this task fails). If a name/order search genuinely returns no matching open ticket for that customer, say plainly 'no existing ticket found' rather than manufacturing one: reporting 'none' for a customer who has none is CORRECT, not a gap. A customer may also have UNRELATED tickets (e.g. an old RMA): only link a ticket that actually concerns THIS stuck shipment, and if none does, report none. Silent-failure gotcha: a missing shipping profile returns unresolved, not a success, never claim a label was created when the draft could not resolve.

RETURNS / PREPAID RETURN LABELS (reverse shipments): there is NO separate 'create return' verb. A return (a prepaid label for goods coming BACK to you, customer→us) is just create_shipment with is_return:true: open a draft from the document that describes the item being returned (shipment_draft_create document_ref=<that item's invoice/order doc id>), then create_shipment(draft_id=<that draft>, offer_code=<a carrier offer>, is_return:true). is_return swaps the addresses (sender=the customer, recipient=your ship-from) and stamps the row kind='return', so it then surfaces in returns_list. Like every create_shipment it is GATED → stage it as PENDING APPROVAL, never a generated label. STAGING A RETURN IS NOT FINISHED UNTIL create_shipment HAS BEEN CALLED, opening the draft, set_package, set_customs and quote are only PREPARATION; the label is staged ONLY by the final create_shipment(is_return:true) call, which returns a blocked/approval envelope. NEVER report a return label as 'staged' / 'pending approval' / 'ready to sign off' unless your LAST create_shipment call actually returned that gated approval. If the draft is still blocked (unresolved: no_profile / a customs article blocked: missing_weight), create_shipment will refuse, so you MUST first clear every block: set_package to give the parcel a real weight/dimensions, and (only if the route is an EXPORT that needs customs) set_customs to give each article its weight/HS code: then re-read the draft (shipment_draft_get) to confirm nothing is blocked, and ONLY THEN call create_shipment to land the approval. A warranty RMA return is exactly this: confirm the warranty, then draft from the customer's invoice → resolve the parcel → create_shipment(is_return:true) GATED → report the pending return-label approval.

ATTACHING AN ALREADY-PREPARED RETURN LABEL TO A CUSTOMER REPLY, when the ask is to reply to a customer (mail or ticket) and ATTACH the return shipping label for an EXISTING prepared return shipment ('reply with the RMA instructions and attach the return label'), you do NOT create a new shipment: the prepared label is stored as a kernel FILE on its shipment row, so the reliable, end-to-end path to a real attachable file id is, (1) find the customer's RETURN shipment with search (query the customer name) or returns_list and read its shipment id (recipient_summary names the customer; kind='return'); (2) call the kernel files_list tool with (app='boxtal', entityType='shipment', entityId=<that shipment id>) to get the label file's id and filename; (3) pass that file id into the reply tool's `attachments` array (mail__reply / tickets__reply attachments=[<that fileId>]). NEVER invent or guess a label/file id, and NEVER tell the customer you attached the label unless the reply call's attachments array actually carried that files_list-returned id (an empty attachments array means nothing was attached: claiming otherwise is a fabrication). get_documents re-mints the live carrier signed-URL view of the documents, but the ATTACHABLE kernel file id for a reply comes from files_list on the shipment, not from a document URL.

WRONG-ITEM / MIS-SHIPMENT RECOVERY = TWO SEPARATE shipments, staged TOGETHER: when a customer got the WRONG item and needs the right one (e.g. ordered a bundle, received a bare accessory), you recover in two distinct legs and you stage BOTH gated proposals in the SAME turn, do NOT do one and defer the other 'until the first is approved' (the operator asked for both; deferring leaves the recovery half-done and the two proposals never pending at once): (1) the RETURN of the wrong item, open a draft from the WRONG item's doc and create_shipment(is_return:true) for the prepaid return label; (2) the RESHIP of the correct item: open a SEPARATE draft from the CORRECT order's invoice and create_shipment (outbound, is_return omitted). Each leg's create_shipment must bind to ITS OWN draft_id: the draft_id is the document id its draft was opened from (the wrong-item doc for the return, the correct-order invoice for the reship); NEVER pass the other leg's draft, and NEVER pass an approval-request id (the 'Request ID' an approval returns is NOT a draft id: passing it makes create_shipment fail to find the invoice). After staging both, your summary MUST clearly distinguish the TWO pending approvals (one return label + one reship), each with which item it covers, not collapse them into one.

TODAY'S BATCH / WHAT TO SHIP: when the ask is about the orders to prepare, classify, or ship today ("today's batch", "the orders awaiting shipment", "what's ready to pack/ship", "classify these for customs", AND the surge-backlog phrasing "pull/grab the (paid) unfulfilled DTC orders from this weekend and stage Boxtal shipments / labels so I can approve a batch" / "the Black Friday backlog: group them by carrier and stage the shipments for batch approval"), the authoritative source is the To-prepare queue (the issued invoices with shippable goods and no live shipment yet): enumerate THAT whole queue (to_prepare_list), not a raw store order search. A store order search (Shopify unfulfilled orders) is a DIFFERENT, broader set and will MISS or mis-cover the prepare-batch; CRUCIALLY, a Boxtal shipment draft opens from an order's ISSUED INVOICE (a shippable, draftable row), so a raw Shopify order that has no issued invoice / no resolved shipping profile CANNOT be drafted: feeding such an order id into shipment_draft_create / set_package just dead-ends (no invoice → no draft). So even when the user says "pull the unfulfilled paid orders", the SHIPPABLE batch you draft + stage from is the To-prepare queue, whose rows ARE the invoice-backed orders ready to ship; read THAT, group its rows by destination/carrier, and stage a gated create_shipment per row. If a narrow store search returns fewer rows than the user described, do NOT conclude the missing ones "don't exist": the prepare queue is the ground truth for the batch. Read the queue once, classify every row it returns, and reconcile against what the user said they have rather than steering them away.

STAGING A BATCH OF SHIPMENTS FOR APPROVAL, ANTI-FABRICATION + ONE-PER-ORDER (the surge-batch ask: "stage Boxtal shipments so I can approve a batch" / "group them by carrier and stage the labels for me to approve"). The deliverable is, per order, ONE pending GATED create_shipment approval, and 'staged' means that create_shipment call ACTUALLY returned its blocked/pending_approval envelope THIS turn, NOT that you intend to. THREE hard rules: (1) NEVER claim an order is 'staged' / 'queued for approval' / 'ready to approve' before its create_shipment call returned the gated envelope, a table of orders marked 'staged' / 'pending approval' that is NOT each backed by a real create_shipment result THIS turn is a FABRICATION and the single worst failure here (the weak model's trap: narrating 'I've staged all 12' after only opening drafts or quoting). If a draft is only opened/quoted, say 'drafted, not yet staged': opening a draft is not staging. (2) ONE create_shipment PER ORDER: do NOT double-stage. If you re-stage an order on a corrected carrier (e.g. you first quoted Chronopost then the user said UPS), the EARLIER create_shipment approval does NOT vanish: it stays pending, so you'd leave TWO approvals for one order. Before you finish, reconcile: the count of PENDING create_shipment approvals MUST equal the number of distinct orders; if an order has a stale/duplicate approval from an earlier wrong carrier, do not silently leave both: call it out so the human declines the stale one (there is no auto-dedupe). Plan the carrier per order FIRST, then stage once. (3) GROUND EVERY ROW + ID IN A REAL RESULT: every order/customer/invoice/approval-id in your final table must come from a tool result THIS turn (the to_prepare_list row + that order's create_shipment approvalRequestId). NEVER invent an approval id, a tracking number, or a 'staged' row for an order whose create_shipment you did not actually call, and never mix a fabricated table with the real one. If a per-turn budget caps how many full draft→create chains you finished, stage the bounded subset for real, then state plainly HOW MANY of the batch you staged vs how many REMAIN (name them) and that the rest need another pass: an honest 'staged N of 12, M remain' BEATS a complete-looking table where some rows are invented. And nothing is shipped until the human approves each one, never say a label was created/bought/shipped.

MORNING FULFILLMENT TRIAGE / WHAT'S READY TO PACK NOW, when the ask is the start-of-day prep read ("what's ready to pack and ship this morning", "flag anything stuck or missing info before I open a box", "my morning fulfillment triage"), the operator wants a SINGLE picture of everything on their plate, which spans THREE queues you MUST all surface, do NOT stop after the to-prepare split: (1) read queue_counts for the badge totals; (2) enumerate to_prepare_list and report the READY count separately from the NEEDS-FIX rows, naming EACH needs-fix invoice with its SPECIFIC per-item reason from the row (a missing customs value, a missing weight, or a missing HS code) so the operator knows exactly what to fix before opening the box, never collapse needs-fix into a bare count; (3) ALSO surface the INBOUND RETURNS, call returns_list (NOT exceptions_list: a return is not a carrier exception) and report the returns count and recipients, because parcels coming BACK are part of the morning's work too. queue_counts' `returns` field is the badge; returns_list is the breakdown: a morning triage that reports ready + needs-fix but OMITS the returns queue is INCOMPLETE (the operator still has to open those boxes). This is a READ-ONLY triage: do NOT create_shipment: staging/printing labels is a later, gated step, not part of the morning look.

BATCH-PREPARING THE READY DOMESTIC / FR-EU ORDERS: when the operator asks to prepare/ship 'the ready domestic ones' / 'today's FR/EU orders' / 'the EU domestic batch' with an economy carrier (Colissimo / Mondial Relay) and queue them for approval, 'DOMESTIC' here means the WHOLE intra-EU CUSTOMS-UNION set, NOT France alone: France AND every other EU customs-union destination (DE, NL, BE, ES, IT, IE, AT, PT, …) all ship customs-free and all belong in this batch. Do NOT narrow 'domestic' to FR and silently leave the DE/NL/BE (and other EU) ready orders out, that is the single most common way this task fails: the operator means every customs-free EU order, and dropping the non-FR EU ones without a word forces them to notice and re-ask. From the To-prepare queue, split each ready row by its destination country: intra-EU customs-union → this domestic batch (Colissimo/Mondial Relay, no customs articles); anywhere OUTSIDE the EU (US, JP, GB post-Brexit, CH, …) → an EXPORT, which needs customs + an international carrier: leave those OUT of the economy-domestic batch (do NOT put Colissimo/Mondial Relay on an export). BOUNDED HONESTY ON FAN-OUT: preparing a shipment is a multi-step chain per order (draft → quote → create_shipment), so several full orders can exhaust the per-turn 10-step/60s budget. Process a bounded handful of the domestic batch this turn, then in your reply EXPLICITLY state HOW MANY you handled vs HOW MANY domestic-ready orders REMAIN (name the remaining destinations), and that the rest need another pass (or offer a routine / spawn_agent fan-out): acknowledge the budget rather than pretending you finished all of them or silently dropping the tail. If the full domestic set DOES fit the budget, prepare them all in one turn and say the whole batch is covered with none remaining. Either way the handled-vs-remaining accounting must be explicit and every order you claim to have queued must map to a real create_shipment approval result.

CUSTOMS ARTICLES (EXPORT vs INTRA-EU), an intra-EU destination (FR/DE/NL and the other EU customs-union members) ships customs-free: no commercial invoice, no HS codes, leave its draft's customs articles alone. An EXPORT destination: anywhere OUTSIDE the EU, which INCLUDES European-but-non-EU countries like the post-Brexit United Kingdom (GB) and Switzerland (CH), as well as the US, Japan, etc.: needs a commercial invoice with a correct HS code on EVERY line. HS codes are PER ITEM CLASS, not per shipment: a musical instrument and its accessory carry DIFFERENT codes, so a draft with mixed lines (e.g. a controller/instrument plus an overlay/cable/case accessory) needs a DIFFERENT code on each line, never copy one line's code onto the others. Do not guess or reuse a code: look up the right HS code for EACH line's item class first (the invoicing hs_codes_lookup library returns the code by description: e.g. an electronic musical instrument vs an electrical-apparatus accessory), then set that per-line code on the draft's customs article by index, and read the draft's customsArticles back to confirm each line ended with its own correct code (and no line left incomplete) before you report them: a narrated code no tool result shows does not count.

QUOTING A DRAFT (carrier selection), once you have a draft, get carrier rates by passing that draft's id to quote (quote draft_id=<id>): the destination route, parcels and content come straight from the draft, so the offers are for the ACTUAL destination. An EXPORT route returns INTERNATIONAL carriers (e.g. UPS/FedEx/DPD international); a domestic route returns domestic carriers. Pick a carrier whose offer SERVES the destination country, never select a domestic-only service for an export (e.g. for a shipment to Japan, do not pick a France-only next-day service). If the quote returns no carrier that serves the destination, say so rather than silently choosing a domestic one.

CARRIER PERFORMANCE / SLA REPORTING (on-time rate, exceptions by carrier): Boxtal has NO analytics/aggregate tool and search has NO date-range/created-between filter (query + limit + cursor only). So a request like 'which carrier had the best on-time rate / fewest exceptions last quarter' CANNOT be answered with an authoritative, server-computed, quarter-scoped rate. What you CAN do honestly, and the EXACT sources for each number (never infer a count you did not retrieve): (a) BLANK-enumerate the fleet via search (offset-paged, bounded: read each row's carrier + tracking_status) to get the per-carrier DELIVERED and total-sampled counts: PAGE through to the end of the bounded sample, do not stop after one page and assume the rest; (b) call exceptions_list for the AUTHORITATIVE EXCEPTION/RETURNED/LOST set (group its rows by carrier for the exception counts: do NOT estimate exception counts from a single search page, which may not have surfaced them). Then TALLY per-carrier delivered-vs-exception counts IN-CONTEXT over that bounded recent SAMPLE, with every count traceable to a search row or an exceptions_list row. You MUST label that tally for what it is: a bounded recent snapshot, NOT an authoritative on-time rate and NOT scoped to an exact date window (search has no date filter, so you cannot isolate 'last quarter'), and point the user to Boxtal's own dashboard for the authoritative period report. NEVER fabricate a precise per-carrier on-time PERCENTAGE (e.g. 'Colissimo 94% on-time') presented as if computed over the full quarter: the data you can reach is a sample of whatever shipments the index holds, not a complete dated population. CRITICAL, tally ONLY the carriers and rows you ACTUALLY retrieved in a tool result: a per-carrier count is only valid if you enumerated that carrier's rows. If you paged only PART of the fleet, do NOT fill in a carrier you never fetched with an invented count: either page further until every carrier appears, or report only the carriers your sample covered and say plainly which ones you could not reach. A tally wrapped in honest caveats is STILL fabricated if its numbers were never returned by a tool. Report real counts from what you enumerated, name the two limits (no aggregate tool, no date filter), and offer the snapshot as directional input for the renegotiation, not a definitive scorecard.

SHIPPING THROUGHPUT & SPEND BY CARRIER (how many did we ship this month + what did we spend by carrier): the DOABLE half is parcel VOLUME by carrier; the IMPOSSIBLE half is shipping SPEND. queue_counts is NOT throughput: it returns {to_prepare, ready, returns, exceptions} as LIVE queue state RIGHT NOW, never 'parcels shipped this month': surface it as current queue state and do NOT present it as a monthly shipped count. For VOLUME by carrier: BLANK-enumerate the fleet via search (offset-paged), PAGE to the end of the bounded sample, and group the hits by their `carrier` (offer_code) field in-context (Colissimo / Chronopost / UPS …). MANDATORY FIRST STEP: for ANY throughput / 'how many did we ship' / volume question you MUST first tool_search boxtal and call queue_counts, and RENDER its actual numbers IN THE USER-FACING REPLY: write out the To-prepare / Ready / Returns / Exceptions figures explicitly (e.g. 'Live queue right now: To-prepare X, Ready Y, Returns Z, Exceptions W'), labeled as LIVE queue state NOT monthly throughput: BEFORE and ALONGSIDE the search-based carrier tally. It is NOT enough to merely CALL queue_counts: if you fetch it but omit the numbers from your reply, the user never sees the authoritative current count and the answer is incomplete. Also do NOT let the queue numbers silently coincide with the carrier-tally total: they are DIFFERENT things (live queue state vs total enumerated volume); present each under its own clear label so they are never conflated. Do NOT answer a throughput question from search alone: queue_counts is the backbone that distinguishes live queue state from historical volume, and a reply that omits it is incomplete even if the search tally is correct. You MUST disclose TWO bounds on the search count: (1) it is the per-turn OFFSET-PAGED SAMPLE you actually reached, and (2) search has NO created_at / ship-date field and NO date filter, so you CANNOT isolate 'this month': the per-carrier counts are total-volume-over-the-sample, and 'this month' is APPROXIMATE; never report a precise authoritative this-month per-carrier count. CONSISTENCY, keep the SAME bounded-sample framing across every turn: once you have called the count a per-turn paged SAMPLE, do NOT later UPGRADE it to 'the entire active fleet / complete / authoritative'. A `nextCursor: null` only means the page you fetched had no further rows from that offset: it does NOT license a fresh-turn claim that you enumerated the WHOLE fleet, and you must NEVER assert completeness in a turn that made no search call to substantiate it. Always frame the tally as the bounded sample you paged. For SPEND by carrier: there is NO per-shipment shipping price / label cost stored anywhere: `declared_value` on a shipment is the declared parcel VALUE (customs/insurance), NOT what was paid to ship it. So shipping SPEND by carrier CANNOT be computed today: do NOT sum declared_value (or any field) and present it as carrier spend, and do NOT invent EUR spend figures. State plainly that monthly shipping-spend by carrier is not recorded and cannot be derived from the data, offer the real per-carrier parcel COUNTS (with the sample/no-date-filter caveat) plus the live queue_counts, and point to Boxtal's own dashboard/invoices for the authoritative spend figures the renegotiation needs.

PICKUP-EXPIRY / RETURN-TO-SENDER CUSTOMER HEADS-UP, when the ask is to chase parcels about to expire at a pickup point (Mondial Relay / point-retrait) and 'draft a heads-up to each customer so we don't get a return-to-sender', the deliverable has TWO halves and the SECOND (the drafting) is where this fails: (1) IDENTIFY: search the fleet, filter to the carrier + REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT, then track each candidate and read its authoritative `pickup_deadline`; the AT-RISK set is ONLY the parcels whose `pickup_deadline` is near today (compare the dates), NOT every parcel at a pickup point: a parcel that just arrived has a far-off deadline and is NOT urgent, so do not over-include it. (2) DRAFT a REAL, per-parcel heads-up message for EACH at-risk parcel: a complete body addressed to that customer with their NAME, the carrier tracking number, the EXACT collection deadline date, and the return-to-sender warning all FILLED IN. A generic unfilled template (placeholders like {{tracking}}/{{deadline}}) is NOT a draft and does NOT satisfy 'draft a heads-up': write the actual filled message per customer. DELIVER each draft as a GATED proposal, never auto-sent: for a customer who ALREADY has an open support ticket, issue the heads-up with tickets__reply on THAT ticket (it lands as a pending approval the human releases: it does NOT auto-send); for a customer with NO existing ticket, the SIMPLE, COMPLETE deliverable is to SURFACE THE FULL FILLED DRAFT TEXT INLINE in your reply (the whole message body addressed to that customer with their name + tracking + exact deadline + return-to-sender warning) for the operator to send: that inline filled draft IS the finished deliverable for a no-ticket customer; do NOT thrash trying to force a gated send for them. Do NOT reach for mail__compose (it is not your channel here) and do NOT fabricate a ticket just to reply to it. You MAY instead tickets__create a real ticket for them and then tickets__reply (gated) if you choose, but the inline draft alone fully satisfies the task, so once you have written the inline filled draft for a no-ticket customer, that customer is DONE; state it as a draft for the operator to send, and move on rather than re-attempting a send that keeps failing. CRITICAL anti-fabrication: NEVER claim a message was 'drafted as a gated send', 'queued', 'pending approval' or 'submitted for approval' unless you ACTUALLY called a send tool (tickets__reply) THIS turn and it returned the gated/approval envelope, a claimed pending-approval with no matching successful tickets__reply call is a fabrication and FAILS the task. If a tickets__reply call errors or does not return an approval envelope, do NOT report it as pending approval: say plainly it did not go through and fall back to the inline filled draft instead. An inline filled draft is reported as exactly that ('here is the draft for you to send'), NOT as a pending approval. And never tell the operator you have 'no way to send / no send tool' if the customer has an open ticket, tickets__reply IS the channel and it is gated. So: per at-risk parcel, produce a filled message AND either a real gated tickets__reply (preferred when a thread exists) or an inline filled draft: one or the other, for every at-risk customer, with the gating stated honestly.

CARRIER POLICY (org-wide, applies to EVERY offer pick, outbound AND return): door-to-door COURIER services only (the carrier collects at the sender's premises and delivers to the recipient's door): DHL, FedEx, or UPS; Colissimo is acceptable ONLY when it is clearly cheaper than every courier option. NEVER pick a relay / dropoff-point / pickup-point service (offers with needs_relay_point=true, or a collection/delivery type of DROPOFF_POINT, PICKUP_POINT, POST_OFFICE): customers and repair returns must not depend on relay points. Among the eligible door-to-door couriers, pick the cheapest that meets any stated deadline.

ORDER-PREP QUEUE (To prepare): the worklist is the set of OPEN, UNFULFILLED Shopify orders, one row per order, NOT one row per issued invoice. An order with no invoice yet is still a row (state needs_document, invoice.state missing), and can be excluded like any other. Rows are keyed by `order_key`: 'so:<shopify order id>' for an order row, 'doc:<document id>' or 'pending:<token>' for an order-less shipment. The row's `document_ref` is its ANCHOR: the document its packages, customs articles and quote derive from, and it can be null. Each row has ONE status set by prep_set_status: to_prepare, validated, or on_hold (a warehouse fact, so it can be set on a row with no document and it disables shipping without touching Shopify).

CATEGORY DECIDES THE SHIPPING DOCUMENT: 'sale' ships on the order's issued commercial invoice; 'repair' (return after repair) and 'gift' (sample) are not sales, so prep_set_category makes the app issue a proforma at the org's nominal value (settings_packaging_policy_get) through the invoicing app, ONE LINE PER PHYSICAL ITEM at real quantities, and re-anchors the row on it. That issue is gated in invoicing, so it can come back pending approval, and the category is then locked until the answer lands. prep_add_shipment creates a row for a parcel with NO Shopify order behind it (a repaired unit going back, a sample to a dealer) on the same proforma path. NEVER ship a repaired unit on the original sale invoice: it declares a commercial sale that is not happening, and the nominal proforma is the document that carries a repaired unit back. prep_list is a free read that resolves NO shipment drafts: a row whose anchor was never synced reports state not_synced, and prep_sync (or prep_list with order_keys) is what resolves it. Passing order_keys reads exactly those rows live, which is the cheap way to re-read one row after acting on it.

SHIPPING PROFILES ARE SHARED BY VARIANTS: a profile (weight, solo dims, short code, category, accessory) has its own id, and each product variant LINKS to at most one profile. Several variants of the same physical item (retail, wholesale, a colour, a channel) should use ONE profile, so a weight or a code changes once. packages_list returns shared_profiles (each with its variants), profiles (one row per variant) and unprofiled_variants (variants seen on rows with no profile). For a variant with no profile, prefer product_profile_link to an existing profile of the same item over creating a duplicate with product_profile_upsert, and never guess a code. product_profile_upsert changes only the fields sent; on a variant whose profile OTHER variants share it is refused with their list unless apply_to_shared:true (the edit moves all of them: ask the user first). Moving a variant that already has a profile with product_profile_link is previewed (the differing fields; it enters the new profile's packs) and needs confirm:true. product_profile_merge folds duplicate profiles into one: call it first WITHOUT confirm to preview which variants move and which fields differ, then with confirm:true; it refuses differing fields unless fields_from names the profile whose values win. product_profile_delete is refused while any variant still links to the profile. Linking never re-resolves rows already resolved: they pick the change up at their next sync (prep_sync).

PACK_UPSERT CARTON_TARE IS FULL REPLACE, NOT A PATCH: pack_upsert always writes every field you send, including carton_tare, and any field you omit is reset to null, never left as it was. So if you are editing an EXISTING pack (renaming it, changing its components, correcting a dimension) and that pack already has a carton_tare set, you must read the pack first with packages_list and pass its current carton_tare back in your pack_upsert call. Omitting it silently clears the tare on a pack that already has one, and the next time that pack merges with a loose leftover item the shipment gets taped twice, the same weight bug this field exists to prevent, and it comes back with no warning.

setupGuide.summary: Boxtal uses two API generations: the legacy EnvoiMoinsCher v1 (key + secret) and the current Boxtal v3 (key + secret). Create a free Boxtal account, generate both key pairs, and pick the matching environment.

steps.text: Create a free account at boxtal.com — use a **test** account for sandbox, a normal account for production.
In your Boxtal account's **API / developer** area, generate your **v3** access key + secret.
Generate the legacy **v1** (EnvoiMoinsCher) key + secret from the same account area.
Paste each pair into **v1 API key/secret** and **v3 API key/secret**.
Set **environment** to `sandbox` (test.envoimoinscher.com / api.boxtal.build) for testing, or `production` for live shipping.

packages_list.description: List Boxtal shipping profiles, packs, and local products.

product_profile_upsert.description: Create or update the shipping profile a product variant uses (weight + solo carton dims). Only the fields you send change: an absent solo dim, category, code or accessory flag keeps its value (null clears a dim or the category). A variant LINKED to a profile other variants share is REFUSED with the list of those variants unless apply_to_shared:true, because the edit changes the profile for all of them (shared_with lists them); to change only this variant, product_profile_unlink it first. An unlinked variant gets a new profile of its own. For a new variant of an item that already has a profile, use product_profile_link instead.

solo_length.description: Solo carton dimension (cm). Omit to keep it; null clears it.

solo_width.description: Solo carton dimension (cm). Omit to keep it; null clears it.

solo_height.description: Solo carton dimension (cm). Omit to keep it; null clears it.

content_category.description: Carrier content category. Omit to keep it; null clears it.

short_code.description: Short operator-facing product code (2-4 chars, e.g. ET2, MP, BS) shown in the prep-grid products summary. Empty string clears it.

accessory.description: Small item laid BESIDE the stack instead of on it (a power supply, a cable): the parcel grows by the height of the tallest such item once, however many there are, and its weight is summed. Alone in an order, these items stack normally. Omit it to keep the stored flag.

label.description: Optional name of the profile shown in the catalog (e.g. the product name). Empty string clears it.

apply_to_shared.description: Required when other variants share this variant's profile: true applies the edit to the shared profile, so every one of those variants changes. Ask the user first, naming the variants the refusal listed.

product_profile_link.description: Link a product variant to an EXISTING shared shipping profile. Use it for a variant with no profile that is the same physical item as one already profiled. A variant that already uses ANOTHER profile is only previewed (ok:false, preview:true, differences between the two profiles, and a note that it enters the new profile's packs) unless confirm:true; show the user the differences before confirming. Rows already resolved are not re-resolved; they use the profile from their next sync.

product_id.description: The variant reference (e.g. the Shopify variant id) as invoice lines carry it.

confirm.description: Only to MOVE a variant that already has another profile: absent or false previews the move (preview:true, the fields that change, a note) and writes nothing; true applies it.

product_profile_unlink.description: Detach a product variant from its shared shipping profile. The profile stays for its other variants; this variant has no profile until it is linked again.

product_profile_merge.description: Merge duplicate shipping profiles into one: every variant of the source profiles moves to the target, then the sources are deleted. Without confirm it only PREVIEWS (moves, differences, profiles to delete) and writes nothing. With confirm:true it refuses when any field differs unless fields_from names the profile (target or a source) whose fields the merged profile keeps.

fields_from.description: Only when the profiles differ: the id of the profile whose field values win.

confirm.description: true applies the merge; absent or false previews it.

product_profile_delete.description: Delete a shipping profile no variant uses. Refused while any variant links to it: unlink those variants or merge the profile into another first.

pack_upsert.description: Create or update ONE named pack (carton) with its box dimensions, gross weight, AND its component bill of materials (the `components` array — the list of SKUs the carton holds). For a BUNDLE/kit pack (a carton that contains several distinct products), the `components` BOM is REQUIRED, not optional: a bundle pack with an empty `components` list is INCOMPLETE. Resolve each component name → its SKU first (use `packages_list`, whose `local_products` gives label↔sku, or a product read) and pass every SKU in `components` — never omit the BOM just because it is the last param. Example for a 4-item Studio Bundle carton: components: [ {product_source:"local", product_id:"RAL-44", quantity:1}, {product_source:"local", product_id:"RAL-WND", quantity:1}, {product_source:"local", product_id:"RAL-CASE", quantity:1}, {product_source:"local", product_id:"RAL-CBL", quantity:1} ]. This is a single pack per call. There is NO bulk/batch pack creation and NO CSV/spreadsheet pack-ingest primitive anywhere in Boxtal: you cannot import a whole list of carton SKUs as packs in one operation. So when handed many carton rows (e.g. a 3PL's rate-sheet CSV of dozens of cartons), do NOT claim you imported them all and do NOT loop pack_upsert until the per-turn step budget kills the turn mid-import (a half-done mess) — instead read the source for the real dimensions, create a HANDFUL of packs to demonstrate the unit path (each from real parsed dims, never invented), then HONESTLY state that the rest must be created one-per-call and propose offloading them to a spawn_agent fan-out or a routine that chips through the remainder.

carton_tare.description: Optional. The shipping carton's own tare in kg, ONLY when gross_weight already includes a tare from a prior carton-ladder stacking calculation (e.g. this pack's weight came straight off a resolver worked example like ET2+MP -> 7.6kg, which already carries a 0.5kg carton tare). Leave unset for a pack whose gross_weight is just its own retail-box weight with no separate shipping-carton tare baked in. This is what lets a later merge (a loose leftover riding into this pack's carton) tare the combined shipment exactly once instead of double-taping it.

components.description: The component bill of materials — every SKU the carton holds. REQUIRED for a bundle/kit pack (one that contains several products); an empty array means the pack has no BOM and is incomplete. One entry per component SKU with its quantity.

product_source.description: Where the SKU lives: "local" for an internal warehouse SKU (from local_products in packages_list) or "shopify" for a Shopify product ref.

product_id.description: The component's SKU (e.g. RAL-44, RAL-WND). Resolve the friendly component name → its SKU first via packages_list.local_products (label↔sku).

quantity.description: How many of this SKU the carton holds (usually 1 for a single-of-each bundle).

pack_delete.description: Delete a pack and its components.

local_product_upsert.description: Create or update a local (non-Shopify) product by SKU.

settings_sender_address_get.description: Read the org's Boxtal ship-from (sender) address and whether it is complete.

settings_sender_address_set.description: Set the org's Boxtal ship-from (sender) address used on every shipment. Provide the FULL address (name, company, email, phone, street, city, postalCode, countryIsoCode). NEVER fabricate or guess these fields — if you were asked to set a warehouse/location but were NOT given its exact street, postal code, and phone, ASK the user for those details FIRST and only call this once you have them. Inventing a ship-from address means EVERY shipment ships from a wrong address.

webhooks_repair.description: Re-register the Boxtal v3 webhook subscriptions (tracking-changed, document-created) with the CURRENT kernel webhook secret, reusing each stored subscription's callback URL. Run this when prod logs show Boxtal webhook deliveries rejected with 'Invalid signature' (401 signature_mismatch): Boxtal is still signing with the secret of an older registration, so tracking statuses and label documents stop syncing into the local index. Idempotent: deletes the stale remote subscription (best-effort) and creates a fresh one per event type. Returns {repaired, failed, webhook_status}. If it reports 'no stored subscription', disconnect and reconnect the Boxtal app instead.

quote.description: Get Boxtal carrier quotes for a route. SIMPLEST PATH (use it whenever you have a draft): pass ONLY `draft_id` — the destination route, parcels and content ALL default from the draft, so you do NOT pass `from`/`to`/`parcels`/`content_code` at all (none are required). `from` always defaults to the org origin; `content_code` is OPTIONAL and defaults from the draft, so NEVER re-quote in a loop thinking a required field is missing — if a quote returns no offers it is a real result, not a schema error. Only for a DIRECT (no-draft) route do you build `to` (as an OBJECT {country, postalCode, city}) and `parcels` (each parcel may carry `quantity` for N identical cartons, e.g. {quantity:5, weight:19,...}; content_code defaults from the org catalog's dominant product content category when omitted). When quoting an existing draft, pass its `draft_id` — the route (destination country/postal/city), parcels and content are taken from the draft so you never re-enter the destination, and the offers come back for the ACTUAL destination (an export route returns international carriers, not domestic ones). Otherwise pass `to` (destination, including the ISO country code) and `parcels` explicitly. EACH OFFER CARRIES BOTH A PRICE AND AN ETA — `price_ht`/`price_ttc` (the carrier cost) AND a `collection_date` + `delivery_date` (the arrival estimate). CHEAPEST-THAT-MEETS-THE-DEADLINE (not absolute cheapest): when the ask constrains delivery speed ('arrives within N business/working days', 'must land by <date>', 'fastest under X EUR'), you MUST filter the offers to those whose `delivery_date` MEETS the deadline FIRST, then pick the cheapest of THOSE — never the absolute-cheapest offer if a faster-but-pricier one is the only one that meets the deadline. Compute the ETA from the offer's own `collection_date`→`delivery_date` dates; when the deadline is in BUSINESS/WORKING days, count weekdays (Mon–Fri) only — a delivery_date that is N calendar days out can be fewer business days, so use the actual dates and exclude weekends rather than eyeballing calendar days (this is the single most common mis-pick: rejecting a carrier that DOES meet the business-day deadline, or accepting the cheapest while ignoring the deadline entirely). ON-PREMISE PICKUP + HOME DELIVERY (collection vs delivery mode): each offer ALSO carries `collection_type` (the raw Boxtal collection-mode code, e.g. "PICKUP" = the carrier collects at the sender's own premises, "DROPOFF_POINT" = the sender must drop the parcel at a relay/post point) and a derived `pickup_at_sender` boolean computed from it. To propose carriers with on-premise pickup AND home delivery, filter offers to `pickup_at_sender === true` (equivalently `collection_type === "PICKUP"`) AND `needs_relay_point === false` (home delivery, not a relay-point drop). When `collection_type` is `null` the offer's collection block was absent from the carrier response, so the pickup mode is UNKNOWN — surface that offer WITH the caveat that its pickup mode could not be determined rather than silently EXCLUDING it from an on-premise-pickup match (excluding it on a null would wrongly drop an offer that might in fact be on-premise). NO BATCH-QUOTE / COST-ROLLUP TOOL: quote is ONE route per call; there is NO tool that quotes many orders at once or sums projected shipping spend across a batch. To total shipping cost over several orders you must quote each one and HAND-SUM the chosen offers IN-CONTEXT. Because a draft→quote chain per order plus the per-turn step/time budget caps how many you can process in one turn, a multi-order 'total what we'll spend' is a BOUNDED SAMPLE, not an authoritative whole-batch figure: process a handful, keep a running total of the offers you actually chose, and DISCLOSE in your reply (a) how many orders you covered vs how many remain, and (b) that creating each label is still a separate GATED create_shipment (a quote is not a booked shipment). NEVER present a hand-summed subset total as the authoritative spend for the entire batch. RETURN (reverse) LEG — quoting a prepaid return label (RMA/warranty, parcel ships customer→you): pass is_return:true (with draft_id, or with the same from/to you would use outbound) — the route is swapped for you, so you still pass the CUSTOMER side as `to`/the draft recipient and the org ship-from stays the configured origin. Pick the offer_code from THAT quote and stage it via create_shipment with is_return:true. RELAY / PICKUP-POINT EXCLUSION: by default the org drops relay / access-point delivery services (a B2C order ships door to door), so a relay offer is never surfaced as the cheapest; pass include_pickup_point:true to include them for a customer who explicitly wants a relay.

draft_id.description: An existing shipment draft id (from shipment_draft_create). When set, the destination route, parcels and content default from the draft — quote the draft directly instead of rebuilding the address.

from.description: OPTIONAL. The ship-FROM party, as an OBJECT (NOT a string): {country, postalCode, city}. Omit it entirely — it defaults to the org's configured origin. Never pass a bare string here.

state.description: State/region code — required only for US/AU destinations.

to.description: The destination party, as an OBJECT (NOT a string): {country (ISO alpha-2), postalCode, city}. OMIT it when you pass `draft_id` — the destination is taken from the draft. Only build it for a direct (no-draft) route quote. Never pass a bare string here.

state.description: State/region code — required only for US/AU destinations.

content_code.description: OPTIONAL. The goods content-category code (Boxtal `code_contenu`, e.g. 'content:v1:10250' for electronics). When you quote by `draft_id` it defaults from the draft, so you do NOT need to pass it. For a direct route, omit it unless the destination is a non-EU EXPORT that needs it; call list_content_categories to get a valid code. Do NOT invent a code or loop re-quoting because you think it is required — it is not.

is_return.description: Set true to quote the RETURN leg (customer→us) of a draft or route: the resolved sender/recipient are SWAPPED before pricing, so the offers are for the parcel coming BACK to you. REQUIRED when quoting a warranty/RMA return label — without it you price the outbound direction, whose carrier set and prices differ. The offer_code you pick from an is_return quote feeds create_shipment with is_return:true (create validates the offer against the SAME leg). Omit (false) for a normal outbound quote.

include_pickup_point.description: Include relay / pickup-point offers (UPS Access Point, point relais, drop-off points) that the org excludes by default. Set true ONLY when the customer explicitly wants a relay delivery; otherwise leave it off so a door-to-door order is never quoted at a relay's (often cheaper) price. No effect when the org policy is already off.

ignore_allowlist.description: Bypass the org carrier allowlist for THIS quote only, to see the FULL carrier market (cheaper non-allowlisted carriers like Chronopost / TNT / Colissimo). Use for ad-hoc exploratory quoting ('is there anything cheaper than our allowlisted UPS/FedEx/DHL?') WITHOUT mutating the org allowlist setting. The allowlist is an advisory guideline, not a hard gate: create_shipment is gated (human-approved) and does NOT refuse a non-allowlisted carrier, so a carrier surfaced only via this flag can still be booked once a human approves. No effect when the org allowlist is already empty (unrestricted).

quote_batch.description: Price a WHOLE BATCH of orders in ONE call and total the projected shipping spend — the cost-rollup tool for a wall of orders (e.g. 'for each of these US orders pick the cheapest carrier that still arrives within 5 business days and total what we'll spend'). Unlike `quote` (one route per call), quote_batch fans out SERVER-SIDE: it opens a draft + quotes EACH order, filters each order's offers to those whose ETA meets the deadline, picks the CHEAPEST within-ETA offer per order, and SUMS the selected prices into one AUTHORITATIVE aggregate `total_projected_spend` — so you do NOT quote one-by-one and hand-total a sample. CHEAPEST-WITHIN-ETA, not absolute cheapest: pass `max_eta_business_days` (e.g. 5) and each order's pick is the cheapest offer arriving within that many BUSINESS days (Mon–Fri, computed server-side from collection→delivery) — an absolute-cheaper-but-too-slow offer is EXCLUDED, and an order with NO offer within the ETA is FLAGGED (`no_offer_within_eta:true`), never silently summed at a slower price. SOURCE OF ORDERS: omit `order_refs` to price the To-prepare worklist (shippable issued invoices with no live shipment yet), optionally narrowed by `destination_country` (e.g. 'US'); or pass explicit invoice/document refs in `order_refs`. BOUNDED HONESTLY: the fan-out is capped by `limit` (default 25 — sized so a normal wall is priced authoritatively in ONE call); a bigger wall is reported as priced N of M via `covered_count`/`total_count` — when `covered_count < total_count`, DISCLOSE that the rest still need pricing in another pass (never present a capped subset as the whole-batch total). READ-ONLY / UNGATED: quote_batch QUOTES + TOTALS only — it creates NOTHING. A quote is a point-in-time ESTIMATE, and buying each label is a SEPARATE GATED create_shipment that needs per-order approval; report the projected total as an estimate and keep the label buys gated (never auto-create shipments from a rollup). Read `aggregate.total_projected_spend` (major units) / `total_projected_spend_minor` (minor units) for the batch total, and the per-order `rows[].selected` for each chosen carrier + price + ETA.

order_refs.description: Explicit invoice/document refs (draft ids) to price. Omit to price the whole To-prepare worklist instead.

max_eta_business_days.description: Pick the cheapest offer whose ETA (collection→delivery) is within this many BUSINESS days (Mon–Fri). Defaults to 5.

destination_country.description: Optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 destination filter (e.g. 'US') — only orders shipping to this country are priced. Applies only when pricing the to-prepare worklist (omit `order_refs`).

limit.description: Hard cap on how many orders this call prices (default 25 — sized so a normal wall is priced in one call). Orders beyond the cap are reported un-priced via covered_count/total_count so a huge wall is bounded, not silently truncated.

shipment_draft_create.description: Start a new shipment draft from an invoicing document — pre-fills parcels + customs from the document snapshot (zero re-entry). document_ref accepts a document UUID, an invoice number, or a Shopify order reference. Works for OUTBOUND shipments (issued sale invoice) AND for RETURN labels: a warranty/RMA return opens its draft from the doc describing the item coming BACK — the ORIGINAL sale invoice for an intra-EU return, or the nominal-value RETURN-FOR-REPAIR proforma for a non-EU return (see the warranty-return-label skill) — then quote and create_shipment both take is_return:true. If some lines resolve to no shipping profile (unresolved), set the parcel explicitly with shipment_draft_set_package before quoting.

lines.description: PARTIAL shipment batch: ship only these invoice lines/quantities now. Each entry names an invoice line id and the units to ship in this batch. Omit for the normal full-invoice shipment. While partial batches are live the invoice stays on the to-prepare worklist with remaining_units; the batch also gets its own customs proforma (customs routes) and a partial Shopify fulfillment.

line_id.description: Invoice line id (from invoicing documents_get lines[].id).

quantity.description: Units of that line to ship in this batch.

shipment_draft_set_package.description: Replace the draft's auto-resolved parcel set with an explicit carton set: ONE carton, OR an ARRAY of cartons for a MIXED multi-carton shipment (e.g. 6 master cartons + 1 + 2). Each carton is supplied one of two ways, PREFER the first: (1) a NAMED PACK from the catalog — `{ pack: "STUDIO-BOX" }` (the pack's name or id; dimensions + gross weight resolved server-side from the catalog; run packages_list first; do NOT copy or invent its dims); (2) an AD-HOC carton not in the catalog — raw `{ length, width, height, weight }` (cm / kg). Any carton may carry `quantity` (N identical cartons), so a whole 9-carton load is ONE call: `override: [{ length:62, width:39, height:36, weight:20, quantity:6 }, { length:62, width:39, height:22, weight:7 }, { length:62, width:39, height:42, weight:14, quantity:2 }]`. The set is multi-parcel end-to-end — every colis is sent to the carrier (packages[]) — so you never collapse a real multi-box shipment into one carton. After this the draft needs a re-quote (quote draft_id=<id>) so pricing reflects the cartons. NEVER overwrite an existing operator carton: when shipment_draft_get shows parcel_override:true, the parcels were deliberately set by a human — keep them and do NOT call this tool again for that draft unless the human asks for a change.

override.description: ONE carton (an object) OR an ARRAY of cartons for a mixed multi-carton shipment. Each carton is a NAMED-PACK reference — `{ pack: "STUDIO-BOX" }` (the pack's name or id; dims/weight resolved from the catalog) — OR an ad-hoc carton's raw dims `{ length, width, height, weight }` (cm / kg), and may carry `quantity` (N identical cartons). Example 9-carton load: `[{ length:62, width:39, height:36, weight:20, quantity:6 }, { length:62, width:39, height:22, weight:7 }, { length:62, width:39, height:42, weight:14, quantity:2 }]`. Use `pack` when the operator names a catalog pack; supply raw dims only for a one-off box. Never invent a named pack's dimensions — reference it by `pack`.

pack.description: A named pack's reference — its name (e.g. "STUDIO-BOX") or id, from packages_list. Its length/width/height/gross_weight are resolved from the catalog, so you never re-key (or invent) the dimensions. Takes precedence over raw dims when present.

weight.description: Ad-hoc carton weight in kilograms (only for a one-off box NOT in the catalog; omit when using `pack`).

length.description: Ad-hoc carton length in centimetres (only for a one-off box NOT in the catalog; omit when using `pack`).

width.description: Ad-hoc carton width in centimetres (only for a one-off box NOT in the catalog; omit when using `pack`).

height.description: Ad-hoc carton height in centimetres (only for a one-off box NOT in the catalog; omit when using `pack`).

quantity.description: N identical cartons of these dims (expanded server-side, capped at 20 total). Omit for a single carton.

items.description: One carton of a mixed multi-carton set: a named-pack ref `{ pack }` OR raw dims `{ length, width, height, weight }`, optionally with `quantity` (N identical cartons).

pack.description: Named pack ref (name or id); dims resolved from the catalog.

quantity.description: N identical cartons of this entry.

shipment_draft_get.description: Read the current draft for a draft/invoice id — returns its parcels and customsArticles (each line's index, tariffNumber/HS code, customs description, declared value, country of origin, and an `incomplete` flag). Use this to VERIFY a draft's customs lines from a real tool result before reporting them as prepped — never claim a line's HS code is set unless this read (or the set_customs result) shows that line's tariffNumber. (get_shipment is for a DISPATCHED shipment's live order/tracking and does NOT return customs articles — use this for draft state.)

draft_id.description: The draft id (the invoice's document ref the draft was opened from).

shipment_draft_set_customs.description: Edit a customs article on the draft by index (correct its HS/tariff code, customs description, declared value, weight, or country of origin). Use this to FIX a mis-classified line — e.g. set tariffNumber to the correct HS code for an accessory vs the instrument. Read the draft's customsArticles first (shipment_draft_get) to get the index + current tariffNumber; the edit persists and the re-derived draft reflects the corrected code.

patch.description: Override a customs article's fields (only those to change).

tariffNumber.description: The HS/tariff code for this article (e.g. '8543.70'). Set this to correct a mis-classified line's HS code.

unitValue.description: Per-unit declared value as a plain number in EUR, the currency Boxtal declares in (e.g. 1 for 1.00 EUR). Setting it clears an fx_unavailable block on that article.

originCountry.description: ISO country of origin for this article (e.g. 'FR').

create_shipment.description: Create a Boxtal shipment from a resolved draft + selected carrier offer. GATED (a human approves) → STAGE it and report it as PENDING APPROVAL, never as already shipped. Staging does NOT require the full structured address: the recipient NAME + COUNTRY come from the invoice, and the human confirms/completes the street/city/postalCode/phone on the approval card before the label is bought — so to stage, call this with just `draft_id` + `offer_code` (plus any address fields you already have). SOURCE THE ADDRESS, do not re-key it: for a Shopify DTC order the customer's full shipping address is on the order — fetch it with shopify__orders_get and read `shippingAddress` (street/city/zip/countryCode/phone), then pass it as `recipient_address`. The address the customer entered at checkout is the canonical source; pull it rather than asking the operator to retype what the store already captured. Only ASK the operator for an address field if it is genuinely absent from the order/record AND cannot be fetched — and if a tool call (e.g. set_package) errors, say so plainly and never claim a draft was modified or addressed when the call did not succeed. When rerouting/staging SEVERAL orders, stage create_shipment for EACH and then give a per-order summary (old carrier → new carrier + the cost). EXPORT SHIPMENTS (the route leaves the customs union — a non-EU destination, so the draft carries customs articles): your PENDING-APPROVAL report to the user is not done after 'staged, awaiting your approval' — for an export you MUST also spell out the export treatment so the operator can sanity-check the paperwork before approving: (1) the tax basis is ZERO-RATED (0% VAT — an export sale, not a domestic-VAT one), (2) a COMMERCIAL INVOICE / customs declaration travels with the parcel carrying the HS code(s) + the declared value (= the invoice line total), and (3) the INCOTERM (e.g. DAP for a prepaid distributor export) that governs who clears customs. State these plainly in the staged summary alongside the HS code and declared value you set. Frame the whole thing as STAGED / pending the human's approval — never use 'dispatched', 'initiated', 'sent', or 'finalize the dispatch' wording, since nothing ships until the human approves. WARRANTY/RMA RETURN pipeline: draft from the original sale invoice (shipment_draft_create) → quote with is_return:true → create_shipment with is_return:true + return_reason + the customer's address/phone (the customer is the SENDER; carriers require their phone). For a NON-EU return leg, follow the warranty-return-label skill: issue a proforma at the org's nominal value (RETURN FOR REPAIR - NO COMMERCIAL VALUE) and open the draft from THAT proforma so customs never sees the sale value. SEQUENCED BUNDLE (one human approval for the whole flow): this tool's result exposes referenceable outputs (boxtal_order_id, tracking_number, label_file_id — the imported label PDF as a kernel file id). Stage the follow-up in the SAME turn by copying the @ref token from this call's blocked envelope `outputs` into the next gated call (e.g. tickets__reply attachments=[<label_file_id token>]) — the human then sees and approves ALL stacked actions in one decision, and each step executes with the real values after approval. label_file_id can be null if Boxtal has not generated the label yet at execution (it is produced asynchronously); recover with import_label_document (standalone, or as the sequenced middle step between create_shipment and the reply so the chain carries the real file id). ALWAYS pass quoted_price_ttc: copy offers[].price_ttc for your chosen offer_code from the quote result — the approval card shows it to the reviewer and a call without it is rejected. WORKLIST TIMING: staging this (pending approval) does NOT remove the order from to_prepare_list / the prep dashboard -- the row leaves ONLY after the approval is EXECUTED (the label is reserved). So when you stage, tell the operator the order stays in the to-prepare list until they approve it. OFFER SELECTION: to ship a prep-dashboard row, stage its `quote.selected` offer (the operator's chosen offer, or the cheapest when none is chosen) -- pass that offer_code + its price as quoted_price_ttc. RELAY / PICKUP-POINT: a relay / access-point offer_code is REFUSED (offer_not_quoted) because the pre-buy re-quote drops relay services; pass include_pickup_point:true only when the customer explicitly wants a relay delivery. CARRIER ALLOWLIST (advisory, NOT a buy-time block): unlike the relay exclusion, the carrier allowlist does NOT refuse a buy -- a non-allowlisted carrier the operator explicitly picked (e.g. Chronopost quoted via ignore_allowlist) still ships once the human approves this gated action, so you never need to add a carrier to the allowlist just to book it once.

email.description: Customer's email, from the ticket/contact. Carriers REQUIRE a contact email on the label (a return 422s without it). Auto-filled from the linked contact record when omitted, but pass it explicitly when you have it.

phone.description: Customer's phone (or use the top-level recipient_phone). Carriers require it for pickup.

is_return.description: Set true to create a REVERSE (return) shipment — a prepaid label for goods coming BACK to you (customer→us). It swaps sender/recipient (sender=the customer, recipient=your ship-from), declares customs reason RETURN, and the row then appears in returns_list. Open the draft from the doc describing the item being RETURNED: for a warranty/RMA return that is the ORIGINAL sale invoice — its already-delivered OUTBOUND shipment does NOT block the return (uniqueness is per (invoice, kind): one outbound + one return may coexist; only a second shipment of the SAME kind is a duplicate). The offer_code MUST come from a quote taken with is_return:true (the offer is validated against the RETURN leg, not the outbound one). Omit (false) for a normal outbound shipment to the customer.

return_reason.description: Free-text reason for the return (e.g. 'wrong item shipped — received Windscreen Pack instead of Studio Bundle'); shown on the return row in returns_list.

quoted_price_ttc.description: TTC price of the chosen offer, copied VERBATIM from the quote that returned offer_code (offers[].price_ttc). REQUIRED: the human approval card always shows the reviewer what the label costs, and execution re-checks it against the live price (a >10% drift rejects the buy so a stale approval can never purchase at a different price).

quoted_currency.description: Currency of quoted_price_ttc (defaults to EUR; Boxtal quotes in EUR).

collection_date.description: Optional carrier pickup/collection date (YYYY-MM-DD). This is what BOOKS the pickup: Boxtal schedules the carrier to collect the parcel at the sender on this date. Omit to use the chosen offer's Boxtal-proposed collection date automatically (the normal case). Only set it to force a specific collection day. Without any collection date the label is still created but no pickup is booked, so an on-premise carrier (FedEx, UPS, DHL, Chronopost home collection) never comes to collect.

lines.description: PARTIAL shipment batch: ship only these invoice lines/quantities now. Each entry names an invoice line id and the units to ship in this batch. Omit for the normal full-invoice shipment. While partial batches are live the invoice stays on the to-prepare worklist with remaining_units; the batch also gets its own customs proforma (customs routes) and a partial Shopify fulfillment.

line_id.description: Invoice line id (from invoicing documents_get lines[].id).

quantity.description: Units of that line to ship in this batch.

include_pickup_point.description: Ship on a relay / pickup-point offer, bypassing the org's default relay exclusion for THIS buy (the customer explicitly wants a relay). Without it, a relay offer_code is refused (offer_not_quoted) because the pre-buy re-quote drops relay services. (The relay exclusion IS a buy-time block; the carrier allowlist, by contrast, is advisory and does NOT block a non-allowlisted carrier the operator explicitly picked.)

external_id.description: Merchant ORDER reference to stamp on the Boxtal shipment (what boxtal__search / boxtal__track read back as `external_id`). Defaults to the linked order name (e.g. "#3332"); pass it only for a shipment with no linked order.

label_format.description: Label geometry to ask Boxtal for. Defaults to the org setting (settings_label_format_set). PDF_10x15 is the bare thermal label; PDF_A4 is an office sheet.

track.description: Where a parcel is now, for the person: live tracking for a Boxtal shipment (latest carrier status + checkpoint message + the carrier tracking_number + a pickup_deadline). Report a parcel with its recipient AND its carrier tracking_number — that number is the operative reference a carrier/customer uses to chase a parcel, so cite IT, never the internal shipment id/uuid. When a parcel is STUCK, don't just report the status — also propose the concrete next action that clears THAT exception so the operator can chase it: a customs hold / EXCEPTION needs the import paperwork submitted or the customs broker contacted; a FAILED_ATTEMPT needs a redelivery rescheduled or the address confirmed; a parcel REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT must be collected before it expires (else it RETURNS to sender) — flag the expiry; a RETURNED/LOST parcel needs the customer contacted and a reship or claim opened. PICKUP-POINT COLLECTION DEADLINE — for a parcel awaiting collection at a pickup/relay point (Mondial Relay / point-retrait, status REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT) the result carries `pickup_deadline`: the AUTHORITATIVE carrier-reported ISO date the recipient must collect it by before the parcel is returned to sender. This is the ONLY trustworthy source for WHETHER a relay parcel is 'about to expire' — to decide which pickup-point parcels are near their deadline, compare each parcel's `pickup_deadline` against today; do NOT estimate or fabricate a deadline from the arrival date or guess one (a deadline you did not read from `pickup_deadline` is fabrication). `pickup_deadline` is null for any parcel not at a pickup point.

id.description: The Boxtal shipment/order id. Must be an actual id, not an unresolved @ref: token (those resolve only inside a sequenced bundle).

get_shipment.description: The shipment record, refreshed: a Boxtal shipment's live order + tracking status.

id.description: The Boxtal shipment/order id. Must be an actual id, not an unresolved @ref: token (those resolve only inside a sequenced bundle).

get_documents.description: Fetch a Boxtal shipment's shipping/customs documents.

id.description: The Boxtal shipment/order id. Must be an actual id, not an unresolved @ref: token (those resolve only inside a sequenced bundle).

search.description: Find a shipment by name, order or number in the local Boxtal shipment index. A BLANK/empty query ENUMERATES every shipment (paged) — use it to sweep the whole active fleet. A non-blank query filters by recipient, order id, tracking number, external id, the lifecycle order_status (PENDING/CONFIRMED/CANCELLED) OR the live delivery tracking_status (e.g. IN_TRANSIT / OUT_FOR_DELIVERY / FAILED_ATTEMPT / REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT / EXCEPTION / RETURNED / DELIVERED) — they are different axes. A tracking_status query matches EXACTLY ONE status string (it is a single-value match, NOT a 'stuck'/'needs-attention' grouping): query='IN_TRANSIT' returns ONLY in-transit parcels and EXCLUDES failed-delivery / pickup-expiring ones, so it is the WRONG way to find stuck parcels. There is NO single status that means 'stuck' — the needs-attention set spans SEVERAL DISTINCT tracking_status values: EXCEPTION (incl. customs hold), FAILED_ATTEMPT (a failed delivery — a DISTINCT status, NOT an EXCEPTION), and REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT (a parcel awaiting collection that may expire). To find EVERY stuck parcel reliably, BLANK-enumerate the fleet and classify each hit's tracking_status in-context (or run one filtered query per stuck status) — never assume one filter or one enum captures them all. Each hit returns the recipient, carrier, order_status, a CACHED tracking_status, the real tracking_number, and the external_id (the ORDER reference / order number this shipment is for — cite THAT for the dossier's order, no separate shopify call needed). The hit's tracking_status is a LOCALLY-CACHED snapshot (last webhook/track write) and MAY BE STALE — it is NOT a live carrier read. Do NOT decide stuck-ness (or skip a shipment as 'delivered/healthy') from this cached field; call track per shipment for the authoritative live status, and for a shipment cached DELIVERED cross-check the open support-ticket queue (a delivered-but-disputed parcel is still stuck). The result also carries a cachedStatusNotice saying exactly this. For a shipment's live carrier checkpoint detail (latest event + message), call track. CARRIER VOLUME / THROUGHPUT BY CARRIER: to tally how many parcels per carrier, BLANK-enumerate (empty query) and PAGE to the end, then group the hits by the `carrier` (offer_code) field in context. Two HARD bounds you MUST disclose when you report such a tally: (1) search exposes NO created_at / ship-date field and NO date-range parameter, so you CANNOT isolate 'this month' (or any period) — the count is over the whole active fleet you paged, a per-turn OFFSET-PAGED SAMPLE, and 'this month' is APPROXIMATE at best; never present it as a precise authoritative this-month count. (2) Each hit's `declared_value` is the declared parcel VALUE (customs/insurance), NOT the carrier shipping spend — Boxtal persists NO shipping-price/label-cost field, so shipping SPEND by carrier CANNOT be computed or summed from this index. Do NOT add up declared_value (or invent a figure) and report it as shipping spend; if asked what was spent by carrier, state honestly that spend is not recorded and cannot be derived, and report only the parcel COUNT by carrier with the sample/period caveat. The result also carries dateBoundNotice and spendNotice saying exactly this. COVERAGE — the result carries a real `total` (the COUNT of ALL shipments matching this query across the whole fleet) alongside `nextCursor`: `total` is your coverage DENOMINATOR. The `results` array is ONE offset page (size bounded by `limit`); `nextCursor` is non-null when more pages remain. To report coverage HONESTLY, cite `total` and how many you actually fetched ('I read N of total parcels'); you have paged the WHOLE fleet ONLY after you have fetched all `total` rows (followed `nextCursor` to null AND your fetched count equals `total`). NEVER claim you 'paged to exhaustion' / 'nextCursor is null' / a fleet count you did not actually retrieve, and NEVER invent a total or assert exhaustive coverage you did not perform — read it off `total`. The result also carries a coverageNotice saying exactly this.

queue_counts.description: Badge counts for the To-prepare, Ready-to-ship and Returns queues, PLUS `exceptions` — the number of shipments in a carrier EXCEPTION/INCIDENT/RETURNED/LOST state (stuck parcels). A non-zero `exceptions` means a parcel is stuck; call exceptions_list (and track on each hit) for the breakdown — NEVER declare shipping healthy off this badge alone when `exceptions` is non-zero. These are LIVE queue counts as of NOW (current state) — NOT historical throughput and NOT 'parcels shipped this month'. queue_counts answers 'what is in each queue right now', never 'how many did we ship over a period'. Do NOT report to_prepare/ready/returns as parcels shipped this month; there is no shipped-this-month count here (the shipment index exposes no date filter — see search). SCOPE: the worklist covers ONLY invoices generated from a Shopify order (the invoice carries a shopify_order_id) — manual, repair, and free-text invoices are never shipping work and are excluded by design.

to_prepare_list.description: Exact counts of what is left to ship, ready against needs a fix: a WORKLIST of issued invoices with shippable goods that have NO live shipment yet, returned as a SERVER-SIDE AUTHORITATIVE PARTITION (not a bounded sample): `total` + `ready_count` + `needs_fix_count` are the exact denominators, and the rows come PRE-SPLIT into `ready_to_prepare` (render THESE as the trustworthy ready-to-pack list) and `needs_fix` (each carries its blocking `reason`). The buckets are DISJOINT — a row is NEVER in both — and cover `total`. `rows` is the combined list (back-compat). ANTI-FABRICATION: enumerate the ready list ONLY from the real `ready_to_prepare[].invoice_ref` values the tool returned — NEVER invent an invoice/order reference to fill a count, and NEVER list a `needs_fix` invoice (e.g. one missing a customs value / weight / HS code) under "ready". If the user wants a clean ready list, output `ready_to_prepare` verbatim and keep `needs_fix` strictly separate. Each row carries `prep_status` — "ready_to_prepare" means the invoice resolves cleanly so you CAN open a draft and stage a (gated) shipment; "needs_fix" means a blocking defect (in `reason`) must be cleared first. CRITICAL: `prep_status:"ready_to_prepare"` is NOT "a shipment is staged / ready to ship / sent" — NOTHING here is staged. It is only a hint that the invoice is draftable. To actually stage a shipment you must open a draft, quote it, and call create_shipment (GATED → pending approval); a draft or quote is PREPARATION, only create_shipment stages the label. Never report a row as shipped/staged off its prep_status — that is fabrication. SCOPE: the worklist covers ONLY invoices generated from a Shopify order (the invoice carries a shopify_order_id) — manual, repair, and free-text invoices are never shipping work and are excluded by design. WORKLIST TIMING: a row leaves this worklist ONLY when a full shipment goes LIVE (create_shipment approved AND executed) -- a merely STAGED / pending create_shipment does NOT remove it. The list is DERIVED from live shipments, so there is nothing to update by hand; after you stage a shipment, tell the operator the order stays here until they approve.

prep_list.description: The ORDER PREP DASHBOARD worklist people see, with offers and status: every to-prepare invoice (issued goods invoice, no live shipment yet) joined with its cached Shopify order name/tags, its auto-derived parcels + products summary, its cached shipping quote (cheapest offer + up to 2 alternates), and its editable category (sale/repair/gift/return) + exclusion state. SCAN: the unscoped list read scans the open Shopify orders live, bounded to the 250 most recent, and joins cached meta with cached quotes. It never calls the Boxtal API and never re-quotes, so it stays fast on a large worklist. Pass order_keys to refresh exactly those named rows live. Call prep_sync to refresh stale or missing Shopify meta and quotes. Each row's `state` is 'ready' (quoted + resolves cleanly), 'needs_fix' (a blocking defect — see `reason`, same as to_prepare_list), or 'quote_missing' (resolves fine but has no cached quote yet — prep_sync it). `quote.stale:true` means the cached quote's route/parcels/category no longer matches the row's current state (an edit happened since the last quote) — re-sync before trusting the price. Filterable by `search` (invoice ref/order name/customer/destination substring), `country`, `tag` (an order tag), `product` (substring of the products summary), and `include_excluded` (defaults to hiding excluded rows). `last_sync_at` is when prep_sync last ran. ANTI-FABRICATION: this worklist mirrors to_prepare_list's honesty rules — a 'ready' row means draftable/quoted, NOT staged; only the gated create_shipment stages a label.
