SCOPE: the worklist covers ONLY invoices generated from a Shopify order (the invoice carries a shopify_order_id) — manual, repair, and free-text invoices are never shipping work and are excluded by design. WORKLIST TIMING: a row leaves this worklist ONLY when a full shipment goes LIVE (create_shipment approved AND executed) -- a merely STAGED / pending create_shipment does NOT remove it. The list is DERIVED from live shipments, so there is nothing to update by hand; after you stage a shipment, tell the operator the order stays here until they approve. Each row's `quote.offers` lists every cached offer (for the offer dropdown) with a per-offer `is_pickup_point` flag; `quote.selected_offer_code`/`quote.selected` is the operator's chosen offer (via prep_select_offer) that staging uses instead of the cheapest, null when unchosen or invalidated by a stale quote. Relay / pickup-point offers are excluded by the org policy (default on) before caching, so they normally do not appear here.

search.description: Free-text substring match against invoice ref, Shopify order name, customer, or destination country.

tag.description: Filter to rows whose Shopify order carries this tag (case-insensitive exact tag match).

product.description: Filter to rows whose products summary contains this substring (e.g. 'AS' for AcmeSound).

include_excluded.description: Include rows the operator has excluded (prep_exclude) from the default view. Defaults to false (excluded rows hidden).

validated.description: Only rows whose validation mark matches. true = the operator-validated rows ("all validated shipments"); false = the not-yet-validated ones. Omit for both.

order_keys.description: ROW-SCOPED read: return ONLY these rows (by order_key), read live and with their shipping drafts resolved. The whole-worklist scan is skipped. This is what a single-row refresh uses.

prep_sync.description: Refresh pass for the order-prep dashboard: for each in-scope row, fetches Shopify order name/tags when missing, and re-quotes the shipping cost when the route/parcels/category changed (a cache-invalidating edit) or the cached quote is older than 12 hours — storing the offers (cheapest first) for the row's shipping estimate + offer dropdown. WRITES local cache rows and makes EXTERNAL calls (Shopify + Boxtal) — this is the ONLY prep tool that talks to a live API; prep_list itself never does. Pass `document_refs` to scope the refresh to specific rows (e.g. immediately after editing one row's package/category, so only that row re-quotes) — omit it to refresh the whole to-prepare worklist. Bounded by `limit` (default 25); the result reports `covered_count`/`total_count` honestly, so when the worklist exceeds the cap, disclose that the remainder needs another pass rather than presenting a partial sync as complete. Never creates a shipment — quoting is estimation only; the label buy stays the separate gated create_shipment. Relay / pickup-point services are dropped by the org exclusion policy (default on) before caching, so a door-to-door row is never re-quoted at a relay's cheapest price.

document_refs.description: Scope the refresh to these document_refs (invoice ids) only, e.g. right after editing one row. Omit to refresh the whole to-prepare worklist (bounded by `limit`).

limit.description: Max rows refreshed in this call (default 25). A worklist larger than this is synced in `covered_count`/`total_count`-bounded passes.

order_keys.description: Scope the refresh to these rows (by order_key) instead of by document_ref.

prep_set_category.description: Set an order-prep row's category, which decides WHICH DOCUMENT the parcel ships on and the Boxtal customs basis. 'sale' ships on the order's issued commercial invoice. 'repair' (return after repair) and 'gift' (sample) are not sales: the app issues a proforma at the org's nominal value (settings_packaging_policy_get) through the invoicing app, with ONE LINE PER PHYSICAL ITEM at real quantities, and re-anchors the row's draft, parcels, customs articles and quote on it. Issuing that proforma is gated in invoicing, so it can come back pending approval, in which case the row waits and shows so. REFUSED with row_locked when a shipment has already been bought against the row's current document, or while a proforma approval is pending. Changing the category invalidates the row's cached quote, so the row is re-quoted automatically.

order_key.description: The prep row key, e.g. 'so:5123456789' or 'doc:<document id>'. Preferred.

document_ref.description: Legacy alternative: the anchor document id of the row.

category.description: The row's category. 'sale' ships on the issued commercial invoice; 'repair' and 'gift' make the app issue a nominal-value proforma and re-anchor the row on it.

prep_select_offer.description: Choose which cached shipping offer a prep-dashboard row stages, ONLY when someone wants an offer other than the cheapest: never call it to book the cheapest offer, since create_shipment already buys the cheapest when no offer is chosen. The operator's pick DRIVES the eventual create_shipment (it buys the chosen offer instead of the cheapest). Pass the offer_code of one of the row's cached quote offers (prep_list returns them under quote.offers), or null to clear the choice (staging then defaults to the cheapest). The offer_code is validated against the row's current cached quote, so a stale/unknown code is rejected. The choice is invalidated with the quote: once the row's route/parcels/category change, prep_list shows quote.selected as null until a prep_sync re-establishes the offer.

document_ref.description: The invoice id (document_ref) of the prep-dashboard row to update.

offer_code.description: The offer_code to select (must be one of the row's cached quote offers, from prep_list quote.offers). Pass an empty string to clear the choice (staging then defaults to the cheapest).

prep_set_address_choice.description: Pick which address a prep row's label goes to when the order's own ship-to and the customer's VERIFIED delivery address differ (prep_list shows address_check.state = differs). Until someone picks, create_shipment refuses to stage that row. choice 'order' ships to the order's ship-to, 'verified' to the verified address (pass its id from address_check.verified_address.id as address_id). A person decides this: never pick on your own judgment, ask the operator which one is right. The pick is voided as soon as either address changes, including while it waits for a person, and the row is held again.

document_ref.description: The invoice id (document_ref) of the prep row.

choice.description: 'order': ship to the order's ship-to. 'verified': ship to the customer's verified delivery address.

address_id.description: With choice 'verified': the verified address id from address_check.verified_address.id.

shown_addresses.description: Set by the server when the pick is staged (the two addresses the approval shows); leave it out.

prep_exclude.description: Dismiss an order-prep row from the default prep_list view (e.g. an order that will not ship through Boxtal). The row is NOT deleted and comes back with `include_excluded:true` — this only hides it from the default operator view. Reversible via prep_restore. Exclusion is per ORDER, so it works on a row that has no invoice yet.

order_key.description: The prep row key, e.g. 'so:5123456789' (a Shopify order row) or 'doc:<document id>' (an order-less row). Preferred: exclusion now works on rows with no invoice.

document_ref.description: Legacy alternative: the invoice id of the row. Resolved to its order_key.

prep_restore.description: Undo prep_exclude — restores a previously-excluded order-prep row to the default prep_list view.

order_key.description: The prep row key of the excluded row to restore.

document_ref.description: Legacy alternative: the invoice id of the row.

ready_list.description: List live (PENDING or CONFIRMED) shipments whose label is ready, for the operator print station. A freshly bought label starts PENDING until Boxtal confirms the order; it still belongs here. Rows come back sorted by when the label was requested, oldest first. The list is complete: every live shipment the carrier has not collected yet, never a sample. Each row carries `packed` (and `packed_at`): the warehouse bench mark set by ready_set_packed, meaning the parcel is boxed and waiting for pickup. Packed is NOT shipped: the parcel is still in the warehouse until the carrier collects it.

print_record_get.description: Read ONE shipment as its print record: the data the organisation's document templates fill (a customs declaration, a certificate, a thank-you letter). invoice {number, date}, order {name, customer, company, email, phone, address}, shipment {carrier_name, carrier_family, tracking_number, tracking_label}, destination {iso2, name}, lines [{description, sku, hts, origin, quantity, value, unit_value, currency, attributes}]. The invoice, customer, address, carrier and lines are a snapshot taken when the label was bought; the tracking number is the row's current one and stays null until the carrier issues it. A value the sources do not hold is null, never guessed: a template prints it as a blank for a person to fill. To print, use the document templates, not this tool.

shipment_id.description: The shipment row id (a ready_list row id).

attention_rules_list.description: List the attention rules: the DATA that decides when a shipment is marked as needing extra paperwork (e.g. a smelt and cast declaration for aluminium entering the USA). Rules are rows, not code, so the set can be grown from a knowledge-base article without a deploy. Each rule carries its conditions, the documents it requires, and the knowledge article it was written from.

attention_rule_upsert.description: Create or update ONE attention rule. Conditions are ANDed and use a closed language: field is one of destination, carrier, category, products, weight, declared_value, items; op is one of eq, in, contains, starts_with, gte, lte. A rule with no condition never fires (a rule that marks every parcel is a mistake, not a wildcard). `documents` is what the parcel NEEDS, never a claim that it has been produced. Set `knowledge_ref` to the knowledge article the rule was written from so the procedure behind the mark stays reachable.

conditions.description: ALL of these must hold for the rule to fire. A rule with no condition never fires.

field.description: destination is the ISO country; products is the summary string (e.g. "1xET2, 2xHC"); weight is kg; declared_value is the customs value.

op.description: Strings compare case-insensitively; in takes a list; gte/lte are numeric.

value.description: A string or number, or a list of strings when op is in.

documents.description: What the parcel NEEDS. Never a claim that the document has been produced.

name.description: As the operator should read it, e.g. "Smelt and cast declaration".

note.description: One short line: where it comes from or what it must contain.

attention_rule_delete.description: Delete one attention rule by id. Prefer setting enabled=false when a rule is only paused (a seasonal carrier requirement), so the wording and its knowledge reference survive.

print_pack_batch.description: Print a SELECTION of ready-to-ship shipments as TWO merged documents: every label in one PDF for the label printer, every invoice in one PDF for A4 (already collated to each destination's copy count). Use it instead of calling print_pack per row when the operator is clearing a batch. Rows whose label or invoice is not ready are reported in `skipped`, never silently dropped.

print_pack.description: Print a shipment's labels and shipping papers: prepare the print-station documents for ONE ready-to-ship shipment as TWO SEPARATE print jobs, never merged into one PDF: (1) the shipping LABEL alone, orientation-normalized server-side (Boxtal labels carry a Letter-landscape /Rotate 270 flag that label printers ignore; the rotation is baked into the page content) for the self-adhesive label printer, and (2) the INVOICE PDF for the A4 printer with the route's required copy count: 1 copy for an EU/domestic route, 3 copies for an export outside the EU. Returns kernel file ids to download each job separately.

shipment_id.description: The ready_list row id (local shipment row id, a UUID) or the Boxtal order id.

returns_list.description: List inbound return shipments (the parcels coming BACK to you — RMA / warranty / exchange returns, kind='return'). Each row carries the customer (recipient_summary), the return reason, the order/tracking status and whether a label is ready — but NO date, transit-duration, or 'days awaiting inspection' field. So you CANNOT age a return from returns_list alone: there is no created/received timestamp on the row. AGING AN INBOUND RETURN (how long it's been awaiting inspection / 'flag any RMA over N days old' / a weekly returns-aging report) — the age comes from the return's LINKED RMA TICKET, not the shipment: for each return, find its RMA/return support ticket (tickets__search q=<the customer name from recipient_summary>, or by the order/RMA reference) and read THAT ticket's created date (its open time) to compute how long the return has been outstanding; flag the ones whose ticket has been open longer than the threshold (e.g. >7 days), and leave the fresh ones unflagged. Because the age join lives on the tickets side, a routine/agent that ages returns MUST hold tickets:tickets:read (and request it in a routine's scope ceiling) IN ADDITION to boxtal:shipments:read — returns_list gives you the return set, the RMA ticket gives you the age. Do NOT invent a transit duration or a 'days old' number that no tool returned; if a return has no matching RMA ticket, say so for that one rather than fabricating its age. There is no separate boxtal:returns:read scope — returns_list is gated on boxtal:shipments:read.

exceptions_list.description: List shipments stuck in a carrier exception state (INCIDENT, RETURNED, or LOST) so the operator can chase them. A healthy fleet returns an empty list — that is normal, not an error. NOTE: this only catches the hard EXCEPTION/RETURNED/LOST states — a FAILED_ATTEMPT or a parcel awaiting collection at a pickup point will NOT appear here. To sweep ALL stuck parcels in ONE call, prefer stuck_list (the single needs-attention queue that returns the UNION of every stuck family — exception + failed_delivery + pickup_expiring — each row pre-labelled with its family + reason, classified server-side). For every stuck parcel, propose the concrete next action that clears it (submit customs paperwork, reschedule a failed delivery, arrange pickup before expiry, open a claim) — don't just report the status. Each row carries external_id (the ORDER reference) alongside the recipient and carrier tracking_number — cite the order ref / tracking number (never the internal shipment uuid), and quote the EXACT tracking_status string returned (do not paraphrase it).

stuck_list.description: The SINGLE needs-attention queue: every shipment in a STUCK state, across ALL families, in ONE call — so you do NOT have to enumerate the whole fleet with search and classify each tracking_status enum yourself. It returns the UNION of the three stuck families exceptions_list does and does NOT catch, each row pre-labelled with its `family` and a grounded `reason`/next-action: (1) family='exception' — the hard carrier states EXCEPTION/INCIDENT/RETURNED/LOST (e.g. a CUSTOMS HOLD), the same set exceptions_list returns; (2) family='failed_delivery' — a FAILED_ATTEMPT (a failed delivery attempt — a DISTINCT status, NOT an EXCEPTION); (3) family='pickup_expiring' — a REACHED_DELIVERY_PICKUP_POINT parcel awaiting collection at a Mondial Relay / point-relais pickup point that will RETURN TO SENDER if not collected. HEALTHY states (ANNOUNCED/SHIPPED/IN_TRANSIT/OUT_FOR_DELIVERY/DELIVERED) and CANCELLED shipments are EXCLUDED — a healthy in-transit / out-for-delivery / delivered parcel never appears here, so it is safe to render every returned row as genuinely stuck. A fully healthy fleet returns an empty list — that is normal, not an error. This is the reliable, single-call way to find EVERY stuck parcel for a sweep or a watcher routine: read stuck_list, then for each row report its family + reason + the ORDER REFERENCE (the `order_ref` field) + carrier tracking_number; for a parcel's LIVE carrier checkpoint detail (or a pickup point's exact collection deadline) you can still call track on that shipment. ORDER REFERENCE: each row carries `order_ref` — the single order reference to cite — which is the merchant `external_id` (e.g. the Shopify order number) when the shipment has one, ELSE the `boxtal_order_id` (the carrier-side Boxtal order id). `order_ref` is ALWAYS tool-backed and is the right value to quote as the order id; the row also exposes the raw `external_id` and `boxtal_order_id` separately. Cite `order_ref` + tracking_number returned (never the internal shipment-row uuid, never an invented number), and quote the EXACT tracking_status string (do not paraphrase it). (4) family='create_orphan': NOT a carrier state. A label purchase whose create call was interrupted before the Boxtal order id was saved, so a paid label may exist at Boxtal with no local record. These rows have no tracking_status and no tracking number; they are only listed once the reservation is at least 15 minutes old, so a create running right now never appears. Report them for a human to check in the Boxtal dashboard: never buy, re-buy or cancel anything in response. Once the person says what the dashboard shows, settle the row with settle_orphan_create (adopt with the Boxtal order id, or release when no label was bought).

settle_orphan_create.description: Settle an orphaned label purchase: a stuck_list row of family create_orphan, whose create call was interrupted before the Boxtal order id was saved. Use it ONLY after a person has checked the Boxtal dashboard and told you what is there; never guess. outcome 'adopt' + boxtal_order_id: an order exists at Boxtal for this invoice; the app reads that order back and links it to the row, exactly as the automatic sweep would. outcome 'release': the person confirmed NO label was bought; the reservation is closed locally (link_state create_abandoned), leaves stuck_list, and the invoice can get a new label. Release never cancels or changes anything at Boxtal and is refused when the row already carries a Boxtal order id. Refused on any row that is not an orphan (a create still running, a created, cancelled or already released shipment). GATED for agents: report it as pending approval, never as done. Pass the row id stuck_list returned as id, and optionally a short note of what was checked.

id.description: The shipment row id of the create_orphan row (the id stuck_list returns).

outcome.description: adopt: Boxtal has an order for it (give boxtal_order_id). release: no label was bought.

boxtal_order_id.description: Required for adopt: the Boxtal order id found in the Boxtal dashboard.

note.description: Optional: what was checked, e.g. 'no order in the Boxtal dashboard for this invoice'.

claim_open.description: Open a carrier claim against a shipment that is in an exception state (incident / lost / returned), e.g. to recover the declared value of a lost parcel. This files (or records, if the carrier claims API is down) a money claim, so it requires human approval — report it as PENDING APPROVAL, never as already filed; never invent a carrier claim reference number. TWO honesty caveats to surface when you file: (1) RECORD-AND-DEGRADE — if the carrier claims API is unavailable the claim is RECORDED LOCALLY with submitted_to_carrier:false (Liaison has it; it is not yet lodged with the carrier); say so rather than implying it reached the carrier. (2) UNINSURED — shipments are created WITHOUT carrier insurance (insurance is not settable at ship time), which may limit how much is recoverable; flag this but still file the claim.

shipment_id.description: Id of the shipment to claim against (must be in an exception state).

amount.description: Claim amount in the shipment currency.

evidence_file_ids.description: Ids of evidence files (photos, invoices) supporting the claim.

cancel_shipment.description: Cancel a Boxtal shipment that has not yet been dispatched. GATED (a human approves), so report the cancellation as PENDING APPROVAL — never as already done. Cancelling only STOPS this shipment; it does NOT re-address or re-ship the goods. So when you cancel to fix a problem with a parcel that still needs to go out (e.g. a wrong/old shipping address), say plainly that a corrected shipment will need a FRESH draft + label afterward (with the right address) — cancellation alone does not deliver the package.

import_shipments.description: Import existing Boxtal orders into the local shipment list by their Boxtal order id (fetches live order + tracking + document descriptors per id; local-only writes, creates nothing at Boxtal). Boxtal's API has no order-list endpoint, so only orders created through this API application are fetchable — web-interface orders cannot be imported.

ids.description: Boxtal v3 shipping-order ids to import (max 20 per call).

import_label_document.description: Backfill-import a created shipment's LABEL PDF into Liaison's file store and return its `label_file_id` (a kernel file id attachable to a tickets__reply / mail message). Boxtal generates the label ASYNCHRONOUSLY after the order, so create_shipment can return label_file_id null — call THIS tool with the boxtal_order_id (or the local shipment row id) to import it once it exists. Retries a few reads internally; returns label_not_ready when Boxtal has not served the LABEL yet (retry in a minute, never fabricate a file id). Also usable as the MIDDLE step of a one-approval sequence: create_shipment -> import_label_document with id = the @ref boxtal_order_id token -> tickets__reply with attachments = [the @ref label_file_id token]. Each call imports a fresh copy; reuse the returned id instead of re-calling.

id.description: The Boxtal order id (from create_shipment's boxtal_order_id / search) or the local shipment row id.

settings_carrier_allowlist_get.description: Read the org's carrier allowlist: the shipping companies (brands) surfaced in routine quoting. Returns `allowed` (the enabled brand keys) and `available` (every selectable brand key + label). An EMPTY `allowed` means NO restriction (every carrier is quoted). When non-empty, ONLY those carriers appear in quotes and the prep-dashboard cheapest. The allowlist is an advisory GUIDELINE, NOT a buy-time gate: create_shipment does NOT refuse a non-allowlisted carrier an operator explicitly picked (the gated human approval is the guardrail) -- so you never add a carrier here just to book it once; add one only to change the ROUTINE default. Each brand covers ALL of that company's service variants (e.g. every FedEx service), so you never enumerate individual services. ALSO returns `exclude_pickup_point_services`: when true (the default) relay / pickup-point delivery services (UPS Access Point, point relais, drop-off points) are dropped from quotes and (unlike the carrier allowlist) ARE refused by create_shipment, so a door-to-door order is never quoted or shipped at a relay price.

settings_carrier_allowlist_set.description: Set the org's carrier allowlist -- the shipping companies (brands) surfaced in ROUTINE quoting (an advisory guideline for the default carrier set, NOT a buy-time gate: create_shipment still ships a non-allowlisted carrier an operator explicitly picked once a human approves). Pass `carriers` as brand keys or names (e.g. ["ups","fedex","dhl"]); each is validated against the known brands (settings_carrier_allowlist_get returns them) and an unknown name is REJECTED with the valid list. A brand covers EVERY service variant of that company (all FedEx/DHL/UPS services), so you never list individual services. Pass an EMPTY list to LIFT the restriction (all carriers allowed again). Note: cached prep-dashboard quotes keep their previously-chosen carrier until a prep_sync re-quotes them. You can also flip `exclude_pickup_point_services` here (relay / pickup-point exclusion, default true) without passing `carriers`.

carriers.description: Brand keys or names to allow, e.g. ["ups","fedex","dhl"]. Empty list = allow all carriers. OMIT to leave the allowlist unchanged (e.g. when only toggling exclude_pickup_point_services).

exclude_pickup_point_services.description: Exclude relay / pickup-point delivery services (UPS Access Point, point relais, drop-off points) from quotes and shipments. Defaults to true. Set false to let relay offers be quoted and shipped. Omit to leave the policy unchanged.

prep_set_validated.description: ALIAS for prep_set_status: mark an order-prep row VALIDATED (true) or return it to 'to prepare' (false). The row carries ONE status (to_prepare / validated / on_hold); prefer prep_set_status, which can also put a row on hold. Does not ship anything and does not change the queue's contents.

order_key.description: The prep row key, e.g. 'so:5123456789'. Preferred.

document_ref.description: Legacy alternative: the invoice id of the row. Resolved to its order_key.

validated.description: true to mark the row validated, false to return it to 'to prepare'.

settings_label_format_get.description: Read the org's default Boxtal LABEL FORMAT (the geometry asked of Boxtal when a shipment is created) plus the selectable formats. PDF_10x15 is the bare 10x15 cm thermal label, ready for a thermal printer; PDF_A4 is an office sheet carrying the label plus carrier boilerplate.

settings_label_format_set.description: Set the org's default Boxtal LABEL FORMAT. Applies to shipments created AFTER the change (a label already bought keeps the format it was issued in). Use PDF_10x15 when labels print on a thermal 10x15 printer: the label then arrives ready to print, with no cropping or rescaling. Use PDF_A4 for an office printer.

format.description: PDF_10x15 (bare thermal label) or PDF_A4 (office sheet).

settings_sender_form_get.description: The settings page's own read of the ship-from address: the stored fields, flat, in the shape settings_sender_address_set takes. Not for agents (settings_sender_address_get is).

settings_form_get.description: The settings page's own read: the pickup-point policy and the label format, in the shape settings_form_set takes back. Not for agents (settings_carrier_allowlist_get and settings_label_format_get are).

settings_form_set.description: The settings page's own write: the object settings_form_get returned with one value changed. Writes only what changed. Not for agents (settings_carrier_allowlist_set and settings_label_format_set are). The ship-from address is not here: the page writes it with settings_sender_address_set.

settings_product_codes_get.description: Read the org's PRODUCT CODE mapping: how raw skus on order line items read as short operator codes in the To-prepare products column (e.g. a wholesale variant `ACME-K1-HARDCOVER-B2B` reading as `HC`, like its retail twin). Returns `strip_prefixes` (house prefixes removed from the front of an sku), `strip_suffixes` (channel suffixes removed from the end) and `aliases` ({sku, code}: a normalized sku, or its trailing product word, and the short code it reads as) and `ranks` ({code, rank}: the display order of the products column in every queue; lower shows first, codes without a rank count as 100, ties alphabetical). All empty by default, in which case skus are shown as they are, in invoice-line order. A product with a shipping profile already reads under its profile's short_code; this mapping is for line items without one.

settings_product_codes_set.description: Set the org's PRODUCT CODE mapping used by the To-prepare products column for line items with no shipping profile. Each field you pass REPLACES the stored one; an omitted field is kept; an empty list clears it. Matching is case-insensitive: one suffix, then one prefix, is stripped, then the result (or its last `-`/`_` word) is looked up in `aliases`. An sku that matches no alias is shown in its stripped form, never dropped. `ranks` sets the ORDER of the products column in every queue, so identical orders read the same: rank: lower shows first; codes without a rank count as 100, ties alphabetical. With no rank set at all the column keeps the invoice-line order. Read settings_product_codes_get first and send the full list you want.

sku.description: The normalized sku (prefix and suffix already stripped) or its trailing product word, e.g. "K1-HARDCOVER" or "HARDCOVER".

code.description: The short code it reads as, 1 to 12 characters, e.g. "HC".

aliases.description: The full alias list. Replaces the stored aliases.

code.description: A short code as the products column shows it (profile short_code or alias code), e.g. "ET2". Case-insensitive.

rank.description: Display rank: lower shows first. Codes without a rank count as 100, ties alphabetical. E.g. 1 to show first, 1000 to show last.

ranks.description: The full display-rank list for the products column of every queue (To prepare, Ready to ship, Returns, Exceptions, Stuck). Replaces the stored ranks; an empty list clears them and restores invoice-line order.

settings_packaging_policy_get.description: Read the org's PACKAGING POLICY: how leftover items (the ones no confirmed pack covers) are boxed when a shipment draft computes its parcels, and the declared value of a nominal proforma. Returns `raw_stack_max_height` (a loose stack up to this thickness in cm ships in its own retail boxes, null = no limit), `cartons` (the carton ladder: each tier's max stack thickness, dimensions, tare weight and `tare_assumed` when the tare is an estimate that must be flagged to the operator; a stack deeper than the last tier fills the last carton, thickest items first, and the remainder starts over), `master_cartons` (applied FIRST: when the units of one product, matched by profile short_code, reach a master carton's `units`, they ship as sealed master cartons at its confirmed dimensions and total gross weight, nothing added), `merge_leftovers_into_packs` and `pack_merge_height_allowance` (whether a leftover stack rides inside a confirmed pack's parcel, and how much deeper a pack plus leftovers may be than a loose stack at the same tier), `nominal_proforma_value_minor` (declared value, EUR minor units, of a return after repair or sample proforma) and `configured`. NEUTRAL DEFAULT when nothing is set: no cartons, so every confirmed pack is its own parcel and all leftover items stack into ONE parcel at their true stacked dimensions and summed weight, with no carton added, no split and no merge; and no nominal value, so a repair or sample proforma is refused until one is set.

settings_packaging_policy_set.description: Set the org's PACKAGING POLICY used by every shipment draft's parcel computation and by nominal proformas. Each field you pass REPLACES the stored one; an omitted field is kept; `reset: true` starts from the neutral default (no cartons, one raw stack, no nominal value). The whole policy is validated before anything is written: carton tiers must ascend by max_stack_height above raw_stack_max_height, and cartons or a pack merge need a raw_stack_max_height. Read settings_packaging_policy_get first. Existing drafts keep their parcels until they are re-derived (prep_sync).

raw_stack_max_height.description: A loose stack up to this true thickness (cm) ships raw, no carton. null = no limit (only without cartons or merge).

max_stack_height.description: Largest true stack thickness (cm) this carton takes, above the previous tier's.

tare_weight.description: The empty carton's weight (kg), added to the stack's weight.

tare_assumed.description: True while tare_weight is an estimate, not a weighed figure: every parcel using this carton then carries a warning.

cartons.description: The full carton ladder, ascending. Replaces the stored ladder; an empty list removes every carton.

short_code.description: The product's short code on its shipping profiles (every variant with this code counts together).

units.description: How many units one master carton holds.

weight.description: Confirmed total gross weight of the packed master carton (kg), contents and carton included.

master_cartons.description: Sealed master cartons, applied before packs and the ladder. Replaces the stored list; an empty list removes them.

merge_leftovers_into_packs.description: Let a leftover stack ride inside a confirmed pack's parcel when the combined thickness fits.

pack_merge_height_allowance.description: Extra height (cm) a pack plus leftovers may reach over each stack threshold, because a pack's height is measured on its own box. 0 by default.

nominal_proforma_value_minor.description: Declared value of a return after repair or sample proforma, in EUR minor units (100 = 1 EUR). null = unset.

reset.description: Start from the neutral default before applying the fields sent.

prep_unlinked_list.description: Shippable orders the To-prepare worklist CANNOT show. The worklist is derived from issued goods invoices carrying a shopify_order_id, so an unfulfilled order with no invoice produces no row at all -- not ready, not needs_fix, not even excluded, just absent with no reason given. That is how a 2 193 EUR B2B order on payment terms sat unshipped and unseen (auto-invoicing fires on PAYMENT, and a terms customer never reaches PAID). This is the counter-check: it lists those orders with WHY each is invisible and WHAT brings it in (issue the goods invoice, then Pull orders). It deliberately returns ORDERS, not worklist rows -- they have no document_ref yet, so none of the draft/quote/ship tools can act on them until an invoice exists. `total` is the number worth watching; `truncated` true means the Shopify scan hit its cap, so treat `total` as a floor.

limit.description: Cap on the Shopify unfulfilled-order scan (default and max 250).

prep_set_note.description: Set or clear the Shopify internal staff note of an order-prep row (the note staff write on the order in Shopify admin; the same text the To-prepare grid shows and edits inline). Only 'so:<shopify order id>' rows carry one: an order-less 'doc:' or 'pending:' row is refused. Pass expected_note (the note the row showed when the operator started editing, or null) so a note someone changed in Shopify meanwhile is NOT overwritten: the call then returns ok:false, reason:'conflict' with current_note, and the caller shows the fresh value. Writes one internal text field on the order: no email, no money, no fulfillment.

note.description: The new note text, or null to clear it.

expected_note.description: Compare-and-set guard: the note the row showed before the edit (null when it showed none). Omit to overwrite unconditionally.

prep_set_status.description: Set an order-prep row's single STATUS: 'to_prepare' (the default working state), 'validated' (the operator has checked the row and cleared it to be prepared and shipped), or 'on_hold' (the row is parked: waiting on stock, on a customer answer, or on a repair). On hold tints and dims the whole row and disables Ship; it does NOT cancel or change anything in Shopify. Rows are keyed by `order_key` ('so:<shopify order id>' for a normal order row, 'doc:<document id>' for an order-less shipment). Setting a status ships nothing and bypasses no guard: a refunded or cancelled order is still refused at create time.

order_key.description: The prep row key, e.g. 'so:5123456789' for a Shopify order row or 'doc:<document id>' for an order-less row.

document_ref.description: Alternative to order_key: the invoice id of the row. Resolved to its order_key.

note.description: Optional short note explaining the status, e.g. why the row is on hold.

prep_add_shipment.description: Create an order-prep row for a parcel that has NO Shopify order behind it: a repaired unit going back to its owner, or a sample going to a dealer. The app issues the row's nominal-value proforma through the invoicing app (one line per physical item, at real quantities) and the row then behaves like any other row: same anchor document, same packages, same quote, same Ship button. Pass `from_order_number` to prefill the recipient and the items from an existing Shopify order, or type the recipient yourself; `recipient` fields override the prefilled ones. Category is 'repair' (return after repair) or 'gift' (sample): an order-less parcel is never a sale, because there is no commercial invoice to ship it on. Issuing the proforma is gated in invoicing, so it can come back pending approval; the row is then keyed 'pending:<token>' and adopts the document as soon as it is issued.

category.description: 'repair' for a unit going back after a repair, 'gift' for a sample.

from_order_number.description: An existing Shopify order number, e.g. '#1042', to prefill the recipient and the items from. Digits only, optionally prefixed with '#': the number reaches a Shopify search query, so anything else is refused rather than searched.

recipient.description: Where the parcel goes. Overrides the prefilled address field by field. Name, street, city, postal code and country are all required in the end.

name.description: Recipient name, as it should read on the label.

company.description: Company name, when the parcel goes to a business.

email.description: Recipient email, for the carrier notifications.

phone.description: Recipient phone in international format. Required by some carriers and by every US and Canada destination.

countryIsoCode.description: Two letter ISO country code, e.g. FR.

items.description: What is physically in the parcel. Defaults to the source order lines when from_order_number is given.

name.description: What the item is, as it should read on the customs declaration.

quantity.description: How many of this item are physically in the parcel.

external_id.description: Catalog reference (Shopify variant id or SKU) so the packages resolve from the shipping profiles.

product_source.description: Where external_id comes from. Defaults to shopify.

hs_code.description: Customs HS code, when it is known.

country_of_origin.description: Country of manufacture, two letter ISO code.

customs_description.description: Customs wording for the item, when it differs from the name.

status_note.description: Optional short note carried on the row.

prep_order_prefill.description: Read what an existing Shopify order would contribute to an ORDER-LESS shipment: its ship-to address and its physical line items. Read only, it creates nothing. Used by the Add shipment panel so the operator sees and corrects the address before the row is created; prep_add_shipment does the same lookup itself when given from_order_number.

order_number.description: The Shopify order number, e.g. '#1042'. A bare number works too. Digits only, optionally prefixed with '#': the number reaches a Shopify search query, so anything else is refused rather than searched.

prep_document_pdf.description: Render an order-prep row's shipping document (the issued commercial invoice, or the app-issued proforma for a repair or sample row) and return the kernel file id of its PDF. Read only. Returns generating:true, not an error, while the PDF is still rendering: that is a wait, not a failure.

order_key.description: The prep row key, e.g. 'so:5123456789'. The row's anchor document is used.

document_ref.description: A document id, when it is already known.

ready_set_packed.description: Tick ONE Ready-to-ship row as PACKED (boxed, taped, waiting for the carrier pickup), which FULFILS its Shopify order with the parcel's tracking number, or untick it. packed:true calls shopify__fulfillments_create for the linked order; the row is only marked packed when the fulfillment succeeds, otherwise `error` says why (no tracking number yet, Shopify refused) and the row stays unpacked. A parcel with no linked Shopify order is marked packed with a `notice` and nothing is fulfilled. packed:false on a fulfilled row CANCELS the Shopify fulfillment and requires confirm_unfulfill:true (without it the call returns error.code confirm_required and changes nothing). From an agent the Shopify calls are gated: the result is error.code pending_approval and the row is NOT packed until a human approves; report it as pending, never as fulfilled.

shipment_id.description: The ready_list row id (local shipment row id, a UUID) or the Boxtal order id.

packed.description: true packs the row and fulfils its Shopify order; false unpacks it (cancelling the fulfillment when the order is fulfilled).

confirm_unfulfill.description: Required with packed:false on a fulfilled row: the operator confirmed cancelling the Shopify fulfillment.

cross_app_calls.reason: mark on Ready to ship which document templates each parcel needs (the organisation's document rules, by SKU, destination and carrier), in one call for the whole list
customs snapshot (HS codes, country of origin, descriptions, declared values) for the invoice→shipment draft hand-off — zero re-entry
enumerate issued invoices for the To-prepare queue (invoices with shippable goods that still need a shipment)

pre-fill the recipient's structured shipping address (street/city/postalCode/phone) from the linked customer's contact record so a gated create_shipment resolves without the operator re-keying what is already on file

read the customer's verified delivery addresses from the contact's address book: a draft compares the order's ship-to with them (match / differs) and ships to a verified address only when the order carries none

prep_sync writes the order's ship-to onto the recipient contact's metadata.shipping_address when it has none (or heals a missing state, phone or email), never overwriting a filled field, so the label buy finds the address; a sync is the app's own write, not an agent's edit
issue the per-batch customs PROFORMA for a PARTIAL shipment (the legal invoice is never split; each batch's proforma covers exactly its shipped lines, keyed idempotently by shipment_ref)

save the operator's inline edit of the order's internal staff note back to Shopify from the To-prepare grid (compare-and-set on the note the grid last showed, so a concurrent edit is refused instead of clobbered)

read the linked order's presentment + shop-currency totals to derive the exact invoice-currency to EUR rate for the customs declaration (Boxtal declares in EUR), and refresh the prep row's order metadata
auto-fulfill the Shopify order when tracking is available; a PARTIAL batch fulfills only its own lines/quantities so the order truthfully shows partially fulfilled
unticking a packed row on Ready to ship cancels the Shopify fulfillment its tick created, after the operator confirms, so the order is never left fulfilled behind a row that reads as not packed

keep ONE pending Shopify fulfillment per parcel: a re-tick withdraws the earlier pending request before staging the current one, and an untick withdraws it, so two approvals for the same parcel can never both be granted
orientation-normalize the Boxtal label PDF (unary merge bakes the page /Rotate into upright content) before serving it to the label printer
render an issued invoice's PDF on demand when the print pack finds it was never rendered (its first render pending or failed), through the invoicing app's own render path
fetch the invoice PDF for the print pack's A4 job (printed 1 copy EU/domestic, 3 copies export)
enumerate every open unfulfilled Shopify order for the To-prepare worklist (the worklist is order-driven: an order with no invoice is still shipping work)
join each open order to its issued documents in one batched call, so the worklist knows which orders have a commercial invoice to ship on without reading each document
resolve the issuer profile the nominal repair/sample proforma is issued under (without it the issue fails issuer_not_found)
read each product's short code from the kernel's provider-neutral product attributes (by SKU) before falling back to the shipping profile's own code
copy each shipping profile's short code onto the SKUs of the variants linked to it (on a profile write, and a daily fill-only backfill), so a store's order list can show it without knowing this app
look up the SKU of a Shopify variant a shipping profile is linked to (cached), to key its short code by SKU in the product attributes

boxtal-overview.description: How to use the Boxtal shipping app with Liaison
boxtal-overview.body: Boxtal connects your shop's orders to carrier shipping labels. Ask the agent to create a shipment for an order and it gathers the parcel weight and addresses, compares carrier offers, and (after your approval) buys the label and stores the tracking number. Set up a routine to poll for orders awaiting fulfilment each morning, or let the agent draft a return label when a customer asks. Knowledge entries about your packaging defaults and preferred carriers help the agent pick sensible offers. Every label purchase is a gated action you approve first.

warranty-return-label.description: Stage a prepaid return label (RMA/warranty): reverse quote, customs proforma, gated purchase
warranty-return-label.body:
Staging a prepaid RETURN label (customer ships their unit back to us — warranty repair, RMA, exchange).

1. Identify the document describing the item coming back. For a warranty repair that is the ORIGINAL sale invoice (or its Shopify order reference). The outbound shipment already recorded on that invoice does NOT block the return: uniqueness is per (invoice, kind), one outbound plus one return may coexist.

2. Decide the customs situation from the ROUTE (customer country → our ship-from country):
   INTRA-EU (e.g. DE→FR): no customs declaration. Open the draft directly from the original sale invoice with boxtal__shipment_draft_create. If the order has NO sale invoice (invoicing__documents_for_orders / documents_search come back empty, or shipment_draft_create throws no_anchor_document because there is nothing to anchor to), create the SAME nominal-value proforma via invoicing__proforma_create_and_issue with the line RETURN FOR REPAIR - NO COMMERCIAL VALUE, and open the draft from THAT proforma PURELY as the anchor. Intra-EU has no customs step, so this proforma is only a draft anchor: do NOT send it to the customer and generate NO customs copies.
   NON-EU leg (customer in UK/US/CH/etc.): customs papers must NOT declare the commercial sale value, or the customer and we get taxed on our own goods coming home. First create and issue a proforma at the org's nominal value (boxtal__settings_packaging_policy_get) via invoicing__proforma_create_and_issue for the returned item, with the line description carrying exactly: RETURN FOR REPAIR - NO COMMERCIAL VALUE. Then open the shipment draft from THAT proforma (document_ref = the proforma), not from the sale invoice, and complete HS code / weight with boxtal__shipment_draft_set_customs if any article is incomplete.
   NO-ANCHOR-DOCUMENT ERROR: if shipment_draft_create returns a no_anchor_document error, the draft has no invoicing document to anchor to. Do NOT retry the call with a different id format (number vs UUID), because the id format is not the problem. Either create the nominal-value RETURN FOR REPAIR - NO COMMERCIAL VALUE proforma described above and open the draft from it, or if you cannot determine the right anchor, STOP and surface the situation to the operator. Never loop retrying the same call.

3. If the draft reports unresolved lines (no shipping profile), set the carton explicitly with boxtal__shipment_draft_set_package (reuse a named pack from the catalog when one fits, e.g. the standard product carton; otherwise ask the operator for weight and dimensions). Never invent weights.

4. Quote the RETURN leg: boxtal__quote with draft_id AND is_return:true. Without the flag you price the wrong direction (our→customer) and the offer will be rejected at staging. OFFER PICK, org carrier policy: door-to-door courier ONLY (the carrier collects the parcel at the customer's address) — DHL, FedEx, or UPS; Colissimo only if clearly cheaper than every courier. NEVER a relay / dropoff-point service (needs_relay_point=true or collection_type DROPOFF_POINT / PICKUP_POINT / POST_OFFICE), even if it is the cheapest offer: a customer returning a unit for repair must get a home pickup, not a trip to a relay point. Among eligible couriers pick the cheapest that meets any stated deadline.

If the draft already shows parcel_override:true, the carton was set by a human operator: keep it, never call shipment_draft_set_package again on that draft.

5. Stage the label: boxtal__create_shipment with draft_id, the offer_code from the is_return quote, quoted_price_ttc (copy offers[].price_ttc for that offer VERBATIM from the quote result; the approval card shows the reviewer the cost and the call is rejected without it), is_return:true, a short return_reason, and the customer's FULL address, EMAIL, and phone in recipient_address (name, email, street, city, postalCode, countryIsoCode) / recipient_phone; email and phone are on the ticket, carriers require both on a return label (the customer is the SENDER of a return; carriers require the sender phone). This tool is GATED: report it as pending approval, never as bought.

6. After the human approves and the label exists, boxtal__get_documents returns the label PDF. Attach it to the ticket reply to the customer, with drop-off or pickup instructions matching the offer's collection type. The shipment then appears in boxtal__returns_list with its return_reason.

7. ONE-APPROVAL SEQUENCE (preferred when the operator asks to handle the whole return in one go): stage the chain in a single turn so the human sees all actions on one approval card. Non-EU: (1) invoicing__proforma_create_and_issue (outputs document_id), (2) boxtal__create_shipment with draft_id set to the proforma's @ref document_id token and is_return:true (outputs boxtal_order_id), (3) boxtal__import_label_document with id set to the @ref boxtal_order_id token (outputs label_file_id — Boxtal generates the label ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so never attach create_shipment's own label_file_id, it can be null), (4) tickets__reply with attachments=[import_label_document's @ref label_file_id token] and the pickup instructions. Intra-EU: skip the proforma, chain create_shipment -> import_label_document -> tickets__reply. Copy each @ref token VERBATIM from the previous call's blocked envelope outputs. Report the whole chain as pending approval; after the human approves, every step runs in order with the real values, and if a step fails the rest is cancelled and you are re-invoked with the context.

8. REPLY WORDING IS CANNED, NEVER IMPROVISED. Before drafting ANY customer message in this flow, read the org's RMA, repair, returns and refund knowledge document (knowledge__search 'RMA return repair') and use its message templates section: template 6.1 when asking the customer for return info (full name, phone, pickup address, serial number), template 6.3 when sending the label. The 6.3 instructions MUST appear in the label reply: photo of the OPENED package with the unit and all accessories before closing; return in original packaging with all included accessories (USB power supply, USB-C cables, MIDI TRS mini-jack adapters, fabric/drum skin if provided); do NOT include separately purchased accessories (mounting plate, extra skins, hard cover); if the original box is gone, use one of equivalent size but no larger (oversized boxes inflate carrier pricing 2X to 3X); attach the label outside the box in a shipping sleeve or under clear tape over the whole label; photo of the sealed package; the carrier-specific pickup line MATCHING the label's carrier, written as the carrier's BASE URL plus navigate to "Schedule a Pickup" (fedex.com / ups.com / dhl.com — deep scheduling URLs differ per country and go stale, so give only the base site; a drop-off location is always the alternative). NEVER tell the customer to call the carrier (phone support does not reliably answer) and never invent a deep URL. The same document is the source of truth for warranty terms, the EU/non-EU proforma routing table, HS codes and the 1 unit repair value, and the refund path (which never gets a prepaid label). SHIPPING THE REPAIRED UNIT BACK. The outbound leg is a row in the To prepare queue, not a second return label. Set that row's category with prep_set_category to 'repair' (return after repair): the app then issues the nominal-value proforma itself, with one line per physical item at real quantities, and re-anchors the row's packages, customs articles and quote on that document. Do NOT ship a repaired unit on the original sale invoice: it declares a commercial sale that is not happening. If the unit never had a Shopify order (a bench unit, a replacement, a sample to a dealer), use prep_add_shipment instead, which creates the row and its proforma on the same path. While the row is waiting on a customer, a part or a bench slot, set prep_set_status to 'on_hold' rather than leaving it looking ready to ship.
